sentences.zh: 冠冕百行莫大於孝，範防百為莫大於義。

translations.literal: Among the hundred conduct of crowned and capped [persons], none is greater than filial piety; among the hundred models and guards of conduct, none is greater than righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Among all virtues, none is greater than filial piety; among all norms of conduct, none is greater than righteousness.

sentences.zh: 先王興孝以教民厚，民用不薄；

translations.literal: The former kings raised up filial piety to teach the people generosity, and the people's use was not stingy;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings promoted filial piety to teach the people generosity, and the people were not mean-spirited;

sentences.zh: 興義以教民睦，民用不爭。

translations.literal: They raised up righteousness to teach the people harmony, and the people's use was not contentious.
translations.idiomatic: They promoted righteousness to teach the people harmony, and the people did not quarrel.

sentences.zh: 率天下而由孝義，非履信思順之世乎。

translations.literal: Leading all under Heaven by filial piety and righteousness—is this not an age of treading in faithfulness and thinking in submission?
translations.idiomatic: When all under Heaven was guided by filial piety and righteousness, was this not an age of faithful conduct and dutiful thought?

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗以來，子有復父仇而殺人者，壯而釋之；

translations.literal: Since Taizu and Taizong, when sons killed men to avenge their fathers, they were admired and released;
translations.idiomatic: Since the reigns of Taizu and Taizong, when sons killed men to avenge their fathers, they were admired and set free;

sentences.zh: 刲股割肝，咸見褒賞；

translations.literal: Those who sliced flesh from their thighs or cut out their livers were all seen and praised and rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: Those who cut flesh from their thighs or excised their livers were all praised and rewarded;

sentences.zh: 至於數世同居，輒復其家。

translations.literal: As for dwelling together for several generations, their households were immediately exempted from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: As for families living together across generations, their households were regularly exempted from labor service.

sentences.zh: 一百餘年，孝義所感，醴泉、甘露、芝草、異木之瑞，史不絕書，宋之教化有足觀者矣。

translations.literal: For more than a hundred years, moved by filial piety and righteousness, the auspicious signs of sweet springs, divine dew, spirit mushrooms, and wondrous trees—the histories never cease recording them; Song's moral transformation has much worth observing.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred years, moved by filial piety and righteousness, sweet springs, divine dew, auspicious mushrooms, and wondrous trees appeared as portents—the records never cease—and the moral transformation of Song is truly worth contemplating.

sentences.zh: 作《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: The 'Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteousness' was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was composed the "Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 李璘，瀛州河間人。

translations.literal: Li Lin was a man of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was a native of Hejian in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，契丹犯邊，有陳友者乘亂殺璘父及家屬三人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era of Jin, the Khitans violated the frontier; there was a Chen You who, taking advantage of the chaos, killed Lin's father and three members of his household.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyun era of Jin, when the Khitans invaded the frontier, a man named Chen You took advantage of the chaos to kill Lin's father and three other members of his household.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，璘隸殿前散祗候，友為軍小校，相遇於京師寶積坊北，璘手刃殺友而不遁去，自言復父仇，案鞫得實，太祖壯而釋之。

translations.literal: In the early Qiande era, Lin was attached to the Palace Front Office as a casual attendant; You was a petty officer in the army. They met north of Boji Lane in the capital. Lin killed You with his own hand and did not flee. He declared that he had avenged his father; the case was tried and found true, and Taizu admired him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qiande era, Lin served as a casual attendant of the Palace Front Office, while You was a petty officer in the army. They met north of Boji Lane in the capital, and Lin killed You with his own hand without fleeing. He declared that he had avenged his father; investigation confirmed the facts, and Taizu admired him and released him.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，又有京兆鄠縣民甄婆兒，母劉與同里人董知政忿競，知政擊殺劉氏。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, there was also Zhen Po'er, a commoner of E County in Jingzhao. His mother Liu had a quarrel with a fellow villager named Dong Zhizheng; Zhizheng struck and killed Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, there was also Zhen Po'er, a commoner of E County in Jingzhao Prefecture. His mother Liu quarreled with a fellow villager named Dong Zhizheng, who struck and killed her.

sentences.zh: 婆兒始十歲，妹方繈褓，托鄰人張氏乳養。

translations.literal: Po'er was at first ten years old; his younger sister was still in swaddling clothes and was entrusted to a neighbor, the Zhang family, to be nursed and raised.
translations.idiomatic: Po'er was only ten years old at the time; his infant sister was entrusted to a neighbor surnamed Zhang to be nursed and raised.

sentences.zh: 婆兒避仇，徙居赦村，後數年稍長大，念母為知政所殺，又念其妹寄張氏，與兄課兒同詣張氏求見妹，張氏拒之，不得見。

translations.literal: Po'er avoided the feud and moved to She Village. Several years later, when he had grown somewhat, he thought of how his mother had been killed by Zhizheng and also thought of his sister lodged with the Zhang family. Together with his elder brother Ke'er he went to the Zhang family to request to see his sister; the Zhang family refused him, and he could not see her.
translations.idiomatic: Po'er fled to avoid the feud and moved to She Village. Several years later, as he grew older, he brooded on his mother's murder by Zhizheng and on his sister living with the Zhang family. He and his elder brother Ke'er went together to the Zhang household to ask to see her, but the Zhangs refused and would not let them.

sentences.zh: 婆兒憤怒悲泣，謂兄曰：「我母為人所殺，妹流寄他姓，大仇不報，何用生為！」

translations.literal: Po'er, angry and weeping in grief, said to his brother: "My mother was killed by another man; my sister is cast adrift and lodged with another surname. If the great feud is not avenged, what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: Po'er wept in grief and anger and said to his brother, "Our mother was murdered, and our sister is living with strangers. If we do not avenge this great wrong, what is the point of going on living?"

sentences.zh: 時方寒食，具酒肴詣母墳慟哭，歸取條桑斧置袖中，往見知政。

translations.literal: It happened to be Cold Food Festival. He prepared wine and food and went to his mother's grave to weep bitterly. Returning, he took a mulberry-wood axe, placed it in his sleeve, and went to see Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: It was the Cold Food Festival. He prepared wine and food, went to his mother's grave, and wept bitterly. Then he returned home, took a mulberry-wood axe, hid it in his sleeve, and went to find Zhizheng.

sentences.zh: 知政方與小兒戲，婆兒出其後，以斧斫其腦殺之。

translations.literal: Zhizheng was just playing with small children. Po'er came out from behind him and with the axe struck his head and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizheng was playing with children when Po'er came up from behind and split his skull with the axe, killing him.

sentences.zh: 有司以其事上請，太宗嘉其能復母仇，特貸焉。

translations.literal: The officials reported the matter upward for decision. Taizong praised his ability to avenge his mother and specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the matter to the throne. Taizong praised him for avenging his mother and specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 徐承珪，萊州掖人。

translations.literal: Xu Chenggui was a man of Ye in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chenggui was a native of Ye in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼失父母，與兄弟三人及其族三十口同甘藜藿，衣服相讓，曆四十年不改其操。

translations.literal: In youth he lost his parents. With three brothers and thirty members of his clan he shared the bitterness of wild greens; they yielded clothing to one another, and for forty years did not change this conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents in childhood. He and his three brothers, together with thirty members of their clan, shared a life of wild greens and coarse fare, yielding clothing to one another, and for forty years never abandoned this way of living.

sentences.zh: 所居崇善鄉緝俗裏，木連理，瓜瓠異蔓同實，州以聞。

translations.literal: At the place where they lived, Chongshan Township, Jisu Lane, trees joined in shared trunks, and melons and gourds of different vines bore fruit together. The prefecture reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In their home village of Chongshan in Jisu Lane, trees grew with conjoined trunks, and melons and gourds on different vines bore fruit together. The prefecture reported these signs.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，詔改鄉名義感，裏名和順。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, an edict changed the township name to Yigan and the lane name to Heshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiande, an edict renamed the township Yigan and the lane Heshun.

sentences.zh: 承珪嘗為讚皇令。

translations.literal: Chenggui once served as magistrate of Zanhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui once served as magistrate of Zanhuang County.

sentences.zh: 劉孝忠，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaozhong was a man of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaozhong was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 母病經三年，孝忠割股肉、斷左乳以食母；

translations.literal: His mother was ill for three years. Xiaozhong cut flesh from his thigh and severed his left breast to feed his mother;
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been ill for three years. Xiaozhong cut flesh from his thigh and severed part of his left breast to feed her;

sentences.zh: 母病心痛劇，孝忠然火掌中，代母受痛。

translations.literal: When his mother's heart pain grew severe, Xiaozhong lit a fire in his palm to take the pain in his mother's stead.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's heart pain grew severe, Xiaozhong lit a fire in his palm to suffer the pain in her place.

sentences.zh: 母尋愈。

translations.literal: His mother soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His mother soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 後數歲母死，孝忠傭為富家奴，得錢以葬。

translations.literal: Several years later his mother died. Xiaozhong hired himself out as a slave to a wealthy family and obtained money to bury her.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when his mother died, Xiaozhong hired himself out as a bondservant to a wealthy family and earned the money for her burial.

sentences.zh: 富家知其孝行，養為己子。

translations.literal: The wealthy family, knowing his filial conduct, raised him as their own son.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy family, moved by his filial devotion, took him in and raised him as their own son.

sentences.zh: 後養父兩目失明，孝忠為舐之，經七日復能視。

translations.literal: Later his adoptive father's two eyes went blind. Xiaozhong licked them for him, and after seven days he could see again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his adoptive father went blind in both eyes, Xiaozhong licked them, and after seven days the man could see again.

sentences.zh: 以親故，事佛謹，嘗於像前割雙股肉，注油創中，然燈一晝夜。

translations.literal: Because of his parents, he served the Buddha diligently. Once before an image he cut flesh from both thighs, poured oil into the wounds, and kept a lamp burning for a day and a night.
translations.idiomatic: Out of devotion to his parents he worshipped the Buddha with great care. Once before a Buddhist image he cut flesh from both thighs, poured oil into the wounds, and kept a lamp burning for a full day and night.

sentences.zh: 劉鈞聞而召見，給以衣服、錢帛、銀鞍勒馬，署宣陵副使。

translations.literal: Liu Jun heard of this and summoned him for an audience, giving him clothing, money and silk, a silver saddle and bridle, and a horse, and appointing him Vice Commissioner of Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun heard of this and summoned him to court, presenting him with clothing, money and silk, a silver saddle and bridle, and a horse, and appointing him Vice Commissioner of Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖親征太原，召見慰諭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Taizu personally campaigned against Taiyuan and summoned him for an audience to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, when Taizu personally campaigned against Taiyuan, he summoned Xiaozhong to court and comforted him with words of praise.

sentences.zh: 呂升，萊州人。

translations.literal: Lü Sheng was a man of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sheng was a native of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 父權失明，剖腹探肝以救父疾，父復能視而升不死。

translations.literal: His father Quan went blind. He cut open his belly and searched out the liver to save his father's illness; his father could see again and Sheng did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Quan went blind, he cut open his own belly and took out part of his liver to cure his father's illness. His father regained his sight, and Sheng himself survived.

sentences.zh: 冀州南宮人王翰，母喪明，翰自抉右目睛補之，母目明如故。

translations.literal: Wang Han of Nangong in Ji Prefecture—his mother lost her sight. Han gouged out his own right eyeball to replace hers, and his mother's eyes were bright as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han of Nangong in Jizhou: when his mother lost her sight, he gouged out his own right eye and placed it in her socket, and her vision was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，並下詔賜粟帛。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, edicts were issued together granting them grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, edicts were issued granting grain and silk to them both.

sentences.zh: 羅居通，益州成都人。

translations.literal: Luo Jutong was a man of Chengdu in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jutong was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 母死，廬墓三年，有甘露降墳樹，芝草生其旁。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he built a hut by her grave and mourned for three years. Sweet dew descended on the grave trees, and spirit mushrooms grew beside them.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he built a mourning hut by her grave and kept vigil for three years. Sweet dew fell on the trees at the grave, and auspicious mushrooms sprang up beside it.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，長吏以聞，詔以居通為延長主簿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, the chief local official reported it, and an edict appointed Jutong as recorder of Yanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao, the local chief reported the matter, and an edict appointed Jutong recorder of Yanzhang County.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，資州人黃德輿葬父母，負土成墳，甘泉湧其側，降詔旌表。

translations.literal: In the early Dazhong Xiangfu era, Huang Deyu of Zizhou buried his parents, carrying earth on his back to form the mound. A sweet spring welled up beside it, and an edict was issued to commend and mark his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dazhong Xiangfu era, Huang Deyu of Zizhou buried his parents, carrying earth on his back to build their mound. A sweet spring welled up beside the grave, and an edict was issued to honor his household.

sentences.zh: 齊得一，密州諸城人。

translations.literal: Qi Deyi was a man of Zhucheng in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Deyi was a native of Zhucheng in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼嗜學，及長，能讀《五經》，善於教授鄉里。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning. When grown, he could read the Five Classics and was skilled at instructing the people of his village.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning from childhood. When he grew up, he could read the Five Classics and was skilled at teaching in his home district.

sentences.zh: 士大夫子弟不遠百里，皆就之肄業焉。

translations.literal: Sons of scholar-officials came from no less than a hundred li away, all going to him to pursue their studies.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of scholar-official families came from as far as a hundred li away to study under him.

sentences.zh: 晉末，皇甫暉為密州防禦使，得一父為客將。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, Huangfu Hui was defense commissioner of Mizhou; Deyi's father served as a guest general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin dynasty, Huangfu Hui served as defense commissioner of Mizhou, and Deyi's father was a staff officer under him.

sentences.zh: 及暉叛歸淮南，屢率眾剽劫於故郡，民之牛羊犬豕悉取以犒士卒，得一之家被略殆盡。

translations.literal: When Hui rebelled and returned to Huainan, he repeatedly led bands to plunder and raid in the former prefecture, taking all the people's cattle, sheep, dogs, and pigs to reward his soldiers. Deyi's household was plundered almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebelled and fled to Huainan, he repeatedly led raiding parties through the old prefecture, seizing the people's cattle, sheep, dogs, and pigs to reward his troops. Deyi's household was stripped nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 後王萬敢為防禦使，性貪暴，執鄉民十八家，責其嘗以牛酒饋賊，盡殺之而取其資產，得一親屬死者十餘人，唯得一與兄脫身獲免。

translations.literal: Later Wang Wangan became defense commissioner. Greedy and violent by nature, he seized eighteen village households, charged them with having once presented cattle and wine to bandits, killed them all and took their property. More than ten of Deyi's kinsmen died; only Deyi and his elder brother escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Wangan became defense commissioner. Greedy and brutal by nature, he arrested eighteen village households, accused them of having once supplied cattle and wine to bandits, killed them all, and seized their property. More than ten of Deyi's kinsmen died; only Deyi and his elder brother escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 明年詣闕上訴，朝廷遣使按鞫之得實，萬敢削官，判官胡轍輒坐死。

translations.literal: The next year he went to the capital to appeal. The court sent an envoy to investigate and try the case; the facts were established. Wangan was stripped of office, and the judge Hu Zhe was immediately sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went to the capital to lodge an appeal. The court sent an investigator, who confirmed the facts. Wangan was stripped of office, and the judge Hu Zhe was immediately put to death.

sentences.zh: 得一乃歸鄉里，布衣蔬食，不樂仕進。

translations.literal: Deyi then returned to his village, wearing plain cloth and eating simple food, and took no joy in pursuing office.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi then returned home, living in plain clothes on simple fare, and had no desire to pursue an official career.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，詔郡國舉廉退孝悌之士，本郡即以得一應詔。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era, an edict ordered the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend men of integrity, modesty, filial piety, and brotherly respect. His home prefecture nominated Deyi in response to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era, an edict ordered the prefectures to recommend men of integrity, modesty, filial piety, and brotherly respect. His home prefecture nominated Deyi in response.

sentences.zh: 至闕，策試中選，授章丘主簿。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he passed the written examination and was selected, and was appointed recorder of Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, he passed the examination and was selected, and was appointed recorder of Zhangqiu County.

sentences.zh: 李罕澄，冀州阜城人也，七世同居。

translations.literal: Li Hancheng was a man of Fucheng in Ji Prefecture; seven generations dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hancheng was a native of Fucheng in Jizhou; seven generations of his family lived together under one roof.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐三年，詔改鄉里名及旌其門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Gan-you of Han, an edict changed the names of the township and lane and marked his gate and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Gan-you of Later Han, an edict renamed the township and lane and honored his household with a commemorative marker.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，長吏以漢所賜詔書來上，復旌表之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, the chief local official presented the edict granted by Han, and he was again commended and marked.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, the local chief presented the edict granted by Later Han, and the household was honored again.

sentences.zh: 刑神留，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Xing Shenliu was a man of Luze in Shenzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shenliu was a native of Luze in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父超，逋官租，里胥督租，與超鬥，超歐里胥死。

translations.literal: His father Chao was delinquent in official grain rent. A village rent collector pressed for collection, fought with Chao, and Chao beat the rent collector to death.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao fell behind on his government land tax. When a village tax collector came to collect the arrears, he fought with Chao, and Chao struck the collector dead.

sentences.zh: 神留年十六，詣吏求代父死。

translations.literal: Shenliu was sixteen years old. He went to the officials and asked to die in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: Shenliu was only sixteen. He went to the magistrate and asked to die in his father's stead.

sentences.zh: 州以聞，特詔減死，賜里胥家萬錢為棺斂具。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported the matter. A special edict reduced the sentence from death, and ten thousand cash was granted to the rent collector's family for coffin and burial supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported the case to the throne. An extraordinary edict commuted the death sentence, and ten thousand cash was granted to the tax collector's family for coffin and burial expenses.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，泰州海陵人沈正父為屯田院衙官，凶暴無賴，使酒毆平人死，正中塗見，父恐懾，述其故，正即號呼褫衣，就毆其屍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong era, Shen Zheng of Hailing in Taizhou had a father who was a yamen runner at the Tuntian Bureau. Fierce, violent, and ruffianly, he got drunk and beat a commoner to death. On the road he met his father; his father was terrified and explained what had happened. Zheng immediately cried out, stripped off his clothes, and went to beat the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era, Shen Zheng of Hailing in Taizhou was the son of a clerk at the Tuntian Bureau. Brutal and unrestrained, he drank himself into a rage and beat a commoner to death. He encountered his father on the road; terrified, the father told him what had happened. Shen Zheng at once shouted, stripped off his clothes, and went to strike the corpse himself.

sentences.zh: 巡警者捕送官，獄具，怡然就死，聞者悲之。

translations.literal: Patrol officers arrested him and sent him to the authorities. When the case was complete, he went calmly to his death. Those who heard of it mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers seized him and handed him over to the authorities. Once the case was settled, he went to his execution with composure, and all who heard of it were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 許祚，江州德化人。

translations.literal: Xu Zuo was a man of Dehua in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zuo was a native of Dehua in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 八世同居，長幼七百八十一口。

translations.literal: Eight generations lived together; old and young numbered seven hundred eighty-one mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations lived under one roof, old and young together numbering seven hundred eighty-one souls.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, his gate and neighborhood were honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, the court honored his household with a commemorative marker at the gate.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，本州言祚家春夏常乏食，詔歲貸米千斛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, the prefecture reported that Zuo's household often lacked food in spring and summer. An edict ordered a yearly loan of a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, the prefecture reported that Zuo's family often went hungry in spring and summer. The court ordered that a thousand hu of grain be lent to them each year.

sentences.zh: 胡仲堯，洪州奉新人。

translations.literal: Hu Zhongyao was a man of Xinfeng in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhongyao was a native of Xinfeng in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 累世聚居，至數百口。

translations.literal: For generations they gathered to live together, reaching several hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation they lived together as one household, until their number reached several hundred.

sentences.zh: 構學舍於華林山別墅，聚書萬卷，大設廚廩，以延四方遊學之士。

translations.literal: He built a study hall at his villa on Mount Hualin, assembled ten thousand scrolls of books, and greatly furnished kitchens and granaries to receive traveling scholars from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At his country estate on Mount Hualin he built a schoolhouse, gathered a library of ten thousand scrolls, and stocked kitchens and granaries on a grand scale to host scholars who came from every direction.

sentences.zh: 南唐李煜時嘗授寺丞。

translations.literal: Under Li Yu of Southern Tang he was once appointed Assistant Director of a Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Li Yu of Southern Tang, he was once appointed Assistant Director of a Temple.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，詔旌其門閭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, an edict honored his gate and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, an edict marked his household gate in recognition of its virtue.

sentences.zh: 仲堯詣闕謝恩，賜白金器二百兩。

translations.literal: Zhongyao went to court to express thanks for the grace shown him and was granted two hundred taels of white-metal vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyao went to the capital to thank the throne for its favor and was rewarded with two hundred taels of silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，州境旱歉，仲堯發廩減市直以振饑民，又以私財造南津橋。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, when drought and famine struck the prefecture, Zhongyao opened his granaries, lowered market prices, and relieved the hungry people; he also used his private wealth to build the Nanjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, when drought and famine afflicted the prefecture, Zhongyao opened his storehouses, cut market prices, and fed the starving; he also built the Nanjin Bridge at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，除本州助教，許每歲以香稻時果貢於內東門。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised this and appointed him Assistant Instructor of the prefecture, permitting him each year to present fragrant rice and seasonal fruits at the Inner East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong commended him, appointed him Assistant Instructor of the prefecture, and allowed him each year to present fragrant rice and seasonal fruit as tribute at the Inner East Gate.

sentences.zh: 五年，遣弟仲容來賀壽寧節。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he sent his younger brother Zhongrong to congratulate the court on the Shouning Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he sent his younger brother Zhongrong to the capital to offer birthday felicitations on the Shouning Festival.

sentences.zh: 召見仲容，特授試校書郎，賜袍笏犀帶，又以御書賜之。

translations.literal: Zhongrong was summoned for an audience and was specially appointed Provisional Collator; he was granted robes, court tablets, and a rhinoceros-horn belt, and was also given imperial calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhongrong for an audience, specially appointed him Provisional Collator, and bestowed on him robes, court tablets, and a rhinoceros-horn belt, along with a scroll of the emperor's own calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 公卿多賦詩稱美。

translations.literal: Many high ministers composed poems praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Many court grandees wrote poems in praise of the family.

sentences.zh: 仲堯稍遷國子監主簿，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Zhongyao was gradually promoted to Director of Studies at the Directorate of Education, retired from office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyao was eventually promoted to Director of Studies at the Imperial Academy, then retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 仲容字咸和，咸平三年，復至闕貢土物，改大理評事，屢被賜齎。

translations.literal: Zhongrong, styled Xianhe, in the third year of Xianping again came to court to present local products, was transferred to the post of Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and repeatedly received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong, whose courtesy name was Xianhe, returned to the capital in the third year of Xianping to present local products, was appointed Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and received repeated gifts from the throne.

sentences.zh: 仲容建本縣孔子廟，頗為宏敞。

translations.literal: Zhongrong built the Confucius temple in his home county, making it quite spacious and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong built the Confucius temple in his home county on a notably grand scale.

sentences.zh: 後遷光祿丞致仕，天禧中，特賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Household Service and retired; in the Tianxi era he was specially granted the crimson fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Household Service and retired; during the Tianxi era he was specially granted the crimson fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 以弟之子用訥為後，試校書郎。

translations.literal: He took his younger brother's son Yongne as his heir and appointed him Provisional Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted his younger brother's son Yongne as his heir and had him appointed Provisional Collator.

sentences.zh: 仲容弟克順，端拱二年進士，至都官員外郎、三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's younger brother Kerun passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Duangong and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Associate Administrator of the Household Bureau in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong's younger brother Kerun passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Duangong and eventually served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Associate Administrator of the Household Bureau in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 仲容子用之洎從子用莊、用舟，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's son Yongzhi, as well as his nephews Yongzhuang and Yongzhou, all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong's son Yongzhi, together with his nephews Yongzhuang and Yongzhou, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 陳兢，江州德安人，陳宜都王叔明之後。

translations.literal: Chen Jing was a man of De'an in Jiangzhou and a descendant of Chen Shuming, Prince of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing was a native of De'an in Jiangzhou and a descendant of Chen Shuming, Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 叔明五世孫兼，唐右補闕。

translations.literal: Shuming's fifth-generation descendant Jian was Right Remonstrating Censor under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Shuming's descendant in the fifth generation, served as Right Remonstrating Censor under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 兼生京，秘書少監、集賢院學士，無子，以從子褒為嗣，褒至鹽官令。

translations.literal: Jian begat Jing, who was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Having no son, he took his cousin's son Bao as his heir; Bao rose to Magistrate of Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Jing served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Having no sons of his own, he adopted his cousin's son Bao as his heir; Bao rose to become Magistrate of Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 褒生灌，高安丞。

translations.literal: Bao begat Guan, Assistant Magistrate of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Guan served as Assistant Magistrate of Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 灌孫伯宣，避難泉州，與馬總善注司馬遷《史記》行於世；

translations.literal: Guan's grandson Boxuan fled to Quanzhou to escape the turmoil and, together with Ma Zong, produced a fine commentary on Sima Qian's 'Records of the Grand Historian' that circulated in the world;
translations.idiomatic: Guan's grandson Boxuan took refuge in Quanzhou during the troubles and, together with Ma Zong, produced an acclaimed commentary on Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian that circulated widely;

sentences.zh: 後遊廬山，因居德安，嘗以著作佐郎召，不起，大順初卒。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to Mount Lu and therefore settled in De'an. He was once summoned as Assistant Editorial Director but did not accept; he died at the beginning of the Dazhun era.
translations.idiomatic: He later traveled to Mount Lu and settled in De'an. Once summoned to serve as Assistant Editorial Director, he declined the appointment and died at the beginning of the Dazhun era.

sentences.zh: 伯宣子崇為江州長史，益置田園，為家法戒子孫，擇群從掌其事，建書堂教誨之。

translations.literal: Boxuan's son Chong served as Long History of Jiangzhou. He further expanded the family estates, established family rules to admonish his descendants, chose clansmen to manage the affairs, and built a hall of books to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Boxuan's son Chong served as Long History of Jiangzhou. He enlarged the family estates, set down household rules for his descendants, selected clansmen to manage family affairs, and built a library hall where they could be educated.

sentences.zh: 僖宗時嘗詔旌其門，南唐又為立義門，免其徭役。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xizong an edict once honored his gate; Southern Tang also established a Gate of Righteousness for the family and exempted them from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xizong, an edict once honored the household gate; Southern Tang later established a Gate of Righteous Kinship for the family and exempted them from corvée service.

sentences.zh: 崇子袞，江州司戶。

translations.literal: Chong's son Gun was Revenue Clerk of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son Gun served as Revenue Clerk of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 袞子昉，試奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Gun's son Fang was Provisional Ceremonial Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gun's son Fang served as Provisional Ceremonial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後兢死，其從父弟旭每歲止受貸粟之半，雲省嗇而食，可以及秋成。

translations.literal: Later, when Jing died, his younger cousin Xu each year took only half the grain on loan, saying that by being frugal in eating they could make it until the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing died, his younger cousin Xu each year accepted only half the grain loan, saying that if they ate sparingly the supply would last until the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 屬歲儉穀貴，或勸其全受而糶之，可邀善價，旭曰：「朝廷以旭家群從千口，軫其乏食，貸以公粟，豈可見利忘義，為罔上之事乎？」

translations.literal: When the year was lean and grain was dear, some urged him to accept the full loan and sell it so as to obtain a good price. Xu said: "The court, considering that the Xu household's extended clan numbers a thousand mouths and taking pity on their lack of food, loaned them public grain—how could one see profit and forget righteousness, and do a deed that deceives one's superiors?"
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine, when grain was costly, some urged him to take the full loan and sell it at a handsome profit. Xu said, "The court, knowing that the Xu clan numbers a thousand souls and pitying their hunger, lent them public grain—how could I chase profit and forget duty, and commit fraud against the throne?"

sentences.zh: 至道初，遣內侍裴愈就賜御書，還，言旭家孝友儉讓，近於淳古。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era, the eunuch Pei Yu was dispatched to grant imperial calligraphy on the spot. On his return he reported that Xu's household was filial, fraternal, frugal, and deferential, close to pure antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao era, the eunuch Pei Yu was sent to present imperial calligraphy in person. When he returned, he reported that the Xu household was filial, fraternal, frugal, and modest—virtues close to those of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗對近臣言之，參知政事張洎對曰：「旭宗族千餘口，世守家法，孝謹不衰，閨門之內，肅於公府。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once spoke of this to his close ministers. Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Bai replied: "The Xu clan numbers more than a thousand mouths; for generations they have kept the family rules, their filial reverence undiminished; within the inner quarters, discipline is as strict as in a government office."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once mentioned this to his close ministers. Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Bai replied, "The Xu clan numbers more than a thousand souls. For generations they have upheld the family code, their filial reverence never slackening; within their household, order is as strict as in a government yamen."

sentences.zh: 且言及旭受貸事。

translations.literal: He also spoke of how Xu handled the grain loan.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the emperor how Xu had handled the grain loan.

sentences.zh: 上以遠民義聚，復能固廉節，為之歎息。

translations.literal: The emperor, [seeing that] distant commoners had gathered in righteousness and could moreover hold fast to integrity, sighed in admiration over it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration that people so far from the capital could live together in righteousness and still hold fast to their integrity.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，以旭為江州助教。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Xu was appointed Assistant Instructor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Xu was appointed Assistant Instructor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 旭卒，弟蘊主家事。

translations.literal: When Xu died, his younger brother Yun took charge of the household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu died, his younger brother Yun took charge of the household.

sentences.zh: 天聖元年，又以蘊繼為助教。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng, Yun was again appointed Assistant Instructor in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiansheng, Yun succeeded him as Assistant Instructor.

sentences.zh: 蘊卒，弟泰主之。

translations.literal: When Yun died, his younger brother Tai took charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun died, his younger brother Tai took over the household.

sentences.zh: 泰弟度，太子中舍致仕。

translations.literal: Tai's younger brother Du was a Retired Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's younger brother Du had retired as Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從子延賞、可，並舉進士。

translations.literal: His nephews Yanshang and Ke both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Yanshang and Ke both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 延賞職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Yanshang was Vice Director of the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 洪文撫，南康建昌人，本姓犯宣祖偏諱，改焉。

translations.literal: Hong Wenfu was a man of Jianchang in Nankang. His original surname violated the taboo character of the Founding Ancestor and was therefore changed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Wenfu was a native of Jianchang in Nankang. His original surname contained a character that violated the taboo of the dynastic founder and was changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諤，唐虔州司倉參軍，子孫眾多，以孝悌著稱。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather E was Revenue Assistant of Qianzhou under Tang. Descendants were numerous, and the family was famed for filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather E had served as Revenue Assistant of Qianzhou under the Tang. The family grew large, and its members were renowned for filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 六世義居，室無異爨。

translations.literal: Six generations lived together in righteousness, and within the household there were no separate cooking fires.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations lived together under one roof, with no separate kitchens in the household.

sentences.zh: 就所居雷湖北創書舍，招來學者。

translations.literal: At the place where they lived beside Leihu Lake he founded a book hall and recruited scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Beside Leihu Lake, where they made their home, he built a library hall and gathered students.

sentences.zh: 至道中，本軍以聞，遣內侍裴愈齎御書百軸賜其家。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, the local command reported the matter, and the eunuch Pei Yu was dispatched bearing a hundred scrolls of imperial calligraphy to grant to the family.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era, the local command reported the family's virtue to the court, and the eunuch Pei Yu was sent with a hundred scrolls of imperial calligraphy as gifts for the household.

sentences.zh: 文撫遣弟文舉詣闕貢土物為謝，太宗飛白一軸曰「義居人」以賜之，命文舉為江州助教。

translations.literal: Wenfu sent his younger brother Wenju to court to present local products in thanks. Taizong granted one scroll in flying-white script reading "Righteous Dweller" and appointed Wenju Assistant Instructor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu sent his younger brother Wenju to the capital with local products to express thanks. Emperor Taizong bestowed a scroll in flying-white script inscribed "Righteous Dweller" and appointed Wenju Assistant Instructor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，又詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, another edict marked their gate and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, another edict honored their household gate.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲遣子弟入貢，必厚賜答之。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever they sent sons and nephews each year to present tribute, the court richly rewarded them in return.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the family sent sons and nephews to court each year with tribute, the throne always responded with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 文撫兄子待用，登咸平二年進士第，至都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Wenfu's elder brother's son Yongdai passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianping and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu's nephew Yongdai passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianping and eventually served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 易延慶字餘慶，筠州上高人。

translations.literal: Yi Yanqing, styled Yuqing, was a man of Shanggao in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yanqing, whose courtesy name was Yuqing, was a native of Shanggao in Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 父贇，以勇力仕南唐至雄州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yun, by valor and strength, served Southern Tang and rose to Prefect of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun entered the service of Southern Tang on the strength of his courage and rose to become Prefect of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 延慶幼聰慧，涉獵經史，尤長聲律，以父蔭為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Yanqing was clever from youth, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially skilled in tonal rules. By his father's privilege he became Ceremonial Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was bright from childhood, read widely in the classics and histories, and excelled especially in prosody. Through his father's privilege he entered office as Ceremonial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，周師克淮南，贇歸朝，授道州刺史；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, when Zhou forces took Huainan, Yun surrendered to the court and was appointed Prefect of Daozhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiande, when the Zhou army conquered Huainan, Yun submitted to the Song court and was appointed Prefect of Daozhou;

sentences.zh: 延慶亦授大名府兵曹參軍，後為大理評事，知臨淮縣。

translations.literal: Yanqing was also appointed Military Administrator of Daming Prefecture, later became Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as Magistrate of Linhuai County.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was also appointed Military Administrator of Daming Prefecture, later served as Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and was appointed Magistrate of Linhuai County.

sentences.zh: 乾德末，贇卒，葬臨淮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qiande era, Yun died and was buried at Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qiande era, Yun died and was buried at Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 延慶居喪摧毀，廬於墓側，手植松柏數百本，旦出守墓，夕歸侍母。

translations.literal: Yanqing was utterly wasted by mourning. He built a hut beside the tomb, personally planted several hundred pines and cypresses, went out by day to guard the grave, and returned at evening to wait on his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was broken by grief. He built a mourning hut beside the tomb, planted several hundred pines and cypresses with his own hands, guarded the grave by day, and returned each evening to attend his mother.

sentences.zh: 紫芝生於墓之西北，數年又生玉芝十八莖。

translations.literal: Purple fungus grew to the northwest of the tomb; several years later eighteen stalks of jade fungus also appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Purple fungus sprang up northwest of the tomb, and several years later eighteen stalks of jade fungus appeared as well.

sentences.zh: 本州將表其事，延慶懇辭。

translations.literal: The prefecture was about to memorialize the matter, but Yanqing earnestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was preparing to report the matter to the throne, but Yanqing firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 或畫其芝來京師，朝士多為詩賦，稱其孝感。

translations.literal: Someone painted the fungi and brought the painting to the capital; many court gentlemen composed poems and rhapsodies praising his filial responsiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Someone painted the fungi and brought the picture to the capital, and many court officials wrote poems and rhapsodies praising the responsiveness of his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，延慶以母老稱疾不就官。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, Yanqing pleaded illness because his mother was old and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, Yanqing pleaded illness on account of his aged mother and declined to take office.

sentences.zh: 母卒後，槁殯數年，延慶出為大理寺丞。

translations.literal: After his mother died, the coffin remained unburied for several years. Yanqing then went out to serve as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he kept her coffin unburied for several years before Yanqing finally took office as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 嘗司建安市征，及母葬有期，私歸營葬，掩壙而返。

translations.literal: He once oversaw market levies at Jian'an. When the date for his mother's burial was set, he privately returned to arrange the burial, sealed the grave, and came back.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as overseer of market levies at Jian'an, he learned that his mother's burial had been scheduled; he left his post without leave, returned home to arrange the burial, sealed the grave, and then went back.

sentences.zh: 知軍扈繼升言其擅去職，坐免所居官，復廬墓側數年。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Hu Jisheng reported that he had left his post without authorization; he was punished by removal from office and again kept vigil beside the tomb for several years.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner Hu Jisheng reported his unauthorized absence, and Yanqing was stripped of office; he then kept vigil beside the tomb for several more years.

sentences.zh: 母平生嗜栗，延慶樹二栗樹墓側，二樹連理。

translations.literal: His mother had loved chestnuts all her life. Yanqing planted two chestnut trees beside the tomb, and the two trees grew with entwined trunks.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had loved chestnuts all her life, so Yanqing planted two chestnut trees beside the tomb; the trees grew together with entwined trunks.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡、朱台符為讚美之。

translations.literal: Su Yijian and Zhu Taifu wrote encomia praising this.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian and Zhu Taifu wrote encomia in praise of the deed.

sentences.zh: 後知端州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Prefect of Duanzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Prefect of Duanzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子綸，大中祥符元年，進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Lun passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 董道明，蔡州褒信人。

translations.literal: Dong Daoming was a man of Baoxin in Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Daoming was a native of Baoxin in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 母死出葬，道明潛匿墓中，人瘞之，經三日，家人發塚取之，道明無恙，終身廬於墓側。

translations.literal: When his mother died and was taken out for burial, Daoming hid himself in the tomb and was buried along with her. After three days the family opened the grave and took him out; Daoming was unharmed, and for the rest of his life he kept vigil beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and was carried out for burial, Daoming hid himself inside the tomb and was buried alive with her. Three days later the family opened the grave and pulled him out; Daoming was unharmed, and he kept vigil beside the tomb for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 郭琮，台州黃岩人。

translations.literal: Guo Cong was a man of Huangyan in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Cong was a native of Huangyan in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，事母極恭順。

translations.literal: He lost his father in youth and served his mother with the utmost respect and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father as a child and served his mother with the utmost respect and obedience.

sentences.zh: 娶妻有子，移居母室。

translations.literal: After marrying and having a son, he moved into his mother's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After marrying and having a son, he moved into his mother's home.

sentences.zh: 凡母之所欲，必親奉之。

translations.literal: Whatever his mother desired, he personally attended to it.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever his mother wanted, he personally saw to it himself.

sentences.zh: 居常不過中食，絕飲酒茹葷者三十年，以祈母壽。

translations.literal: Ordinarily he ate no more than one meal a day, and for thirty years abstained from wine and meat to pray for his mother's longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He ordinarily ate only one meal a day and, for thirty years, abstained from wine and meat in prayer for his mother's long life.

sentences.zh: 母年百歲，耳目不衰，飲食不減，鄉里異之。

translations.literal: When his mother reached a hundred years, her hearing and sight did not fail and her appetite did not diminish; the village marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother reached a hundred, her hearing and sight remained keen and her appetite undiminished, and the whole village wondered at it.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，詔書存恤孝悌，鄉老陳讚率同里四十人狀琮事於轉運使以聞，有詔旌表門閭，除其徭役。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, an edict ordered care and relief for the filial and brotherly. The village elder Chen Zan led forty men of the same neighborhood in submitting a memorial on Cong's conduct to the transport commissioner, who reported it. An edict honored and marked their gate and neighborhood and exempted them from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao, an edict called for the care and honoring of the filial and fraternal. The village elder Chen Zan led forty neighbors in submitting a report on Cong's conduct to the transport commissioner, who forwarded it to the throne. An edict marked the household gate in recognition and exempted the family from corvée service.

sentences.zh: 明年，母無疾而終。

translations.literal: The next year, his mother died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, his mother died peacefully, without illness.

sentences.zh: 琮哀號幾乎滅性，鄉閭率金帛以助葬。

translations.literal: Cong wailed in grief until he nearly destroyed his nature; neighbors contributed gold and silk to aid the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wailed until grief nearly destroyed him, and the neighbors pooled gold and silk to help with the burial.

sentences.zh: 又有越州應天寺僧者，幼貧無以養母，剃髮乞食以給晨夕。

translations.literal: There was also a monk of Yingtian Temple in Yuezhou who, from youth, was too poor to support his mother; he shaved his head and begged for food to supply morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a monk at Yingtian Temple in Yuezhou who, from childhood, was too poor to support his mother; he shaved his head and begged for alms to feed her morning and night.

sentences.zh: 母年一百五歲而終。

translations.literal: His mother died at the age of one hundred five.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived to one hundred five and then died.

sentences.zh: 潭州長沙人畢讚，仕郡為引讚吏，性至孝，父母皆年八十餘。

translations.literal: Bi Zan of Changsha in Tanzhou served the prefecture as usher clerk. By nature he was extremely filial; both parents were over eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zan of Changsha in Tanzhou served the prefecture as an usher clerk. Deeply filial by nature, he had parents both in their eighties.

sentences.zh: 轉運使表其事，詔讚解職終養。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner memorialized the matter, and an edict released Zan from office so that he could care for them to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner reported the case, and an edict released Zan from office so that he could devote himself to caring for his parents until the end.

sentences.zh: 顧忻，泰州泰興人。

translations.literal: Gu Xin was a man of Taixing in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xin was a native of Taixing in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲喪父，以母病，葷辛不入口者十載。

translations.literal: He lost his father at ten. Because his mother was ill, for ten years he did not let pungent or strong flavors enter his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of ten. Because his mother was ill, for ten years he ate no meat or pungent food.

sentences.zh: 雞初鳴，具冠帶率妻子詣母之室，問其所欲，如此五十年，未嘗離母左右。

translations.literal: At the first cockcrow he put on cap and sash, led his wife and children to his mother's chamber, and asked what she desired. Thus for fifty years he never left his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: At the first cockcrow he dressed in cap and sash, led his wife and children to his mother's room, and asked what she wished. He did this for fifty years and never left his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 母老，目不能睹物，忻日夜號泣祈天，刺血寫佛經數卷。

translations.literal: When his mother grew old and could not see objects, Xin wept and cried day and night, invoking Heaven, and pricked his blood to copy several scrolls of Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old and lost her sight, Xin wept day and night, praying to Heaven, and copied several scrolls of Buddhist scriptures in his own blood.

sentences.zh: 母目忽明，燭下能縫衽，九十餘無疾而終。

translations.literal: His mother's eyes suddenly cleared; by lamplight she could sew garments, and at over ninety she died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's eyes suddenly regained their sight; by lamplight she could sew again, and she died peacefully in her nineties without illness.

sentences.zh: 又有杭州仁和人李瓊，以鬻繒為業，事母孝，夜常十餘起省母。

translations.literal: There was also Li Qiong of Renhe in Hangzhou, who made his living selling silk. He served his mother filially and often rose more than ten times each night to look in on her.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Qiong of Renhe in Hangzhou, who earned his living selling silk. Filial toward his mother, he often got up more than ten times each night to check on her.

sentences.zh: 母喜食時新，瓊百方求市，得必十倍酬其直。

translations.literal: His mother loved to eat seasonal delicacies. Qiong sought them in every way at market, and whenever he obtained them he always paid ten times the price.
translations.idiomatic: His mother loved seasonal delicacies. Qiong searched everywhere to buy them, and whenever he found them he paid ten times the going price.

sentences.zh: 朱泰，湖州武康人。

translations.literal: Zhu Tai was a man of Wukang in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tai was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧，鬻薪養母，常適數十里外易甘旨以奉母。

translations.literal: His family was poor. He sold firewood to support his mother and often went several tens of li away to exchange for delicacies to offer his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. He sold firewood to support his mother and often traveled dozens of li to obtain delicacies for her.

sentences.zh: 泰服食粗糲，戒妻子常候母色。

translations.literal: Tai ate coarse and plain food himself and warned his wife and children always to watch his mother's countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Tai ate coarse fare himself and told his wife and children always to watch his mother's mood.

sentences.zh: 一日，雞初鳴入山，及明，憩於山足，遇虎搏攫負之而去。

translations.literal: One day, at the first cockcrow he entered the mountains. By dawn he was resting at the foot of the mountain when he met a tiger that seized and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: One day, at the first cockcrow, he entered the mountains. By dawn he was resting at the foot of the slope when a tiger seized him and carried him away.

sentences.zh: 泰已瞑眩，行百餘步，忽稍醒，厲聲曰：「虎為暴食我，所恨母無托爾！」

translations.literal: Tai had already fallen unconscious. After more than a hundred steps he suddenly woke a little and cried out sharply, "Tiger, if you must gluttonously eat me, what I regret is that my mother will have no one to rely on!"
translations.idiomatic: Tai had already lost consciousness. After more than a hundred paces he suddenly came partly to his senses and cried out, "Tiger, if you must devour me, what I regret is that my mother will have no one to depend on!"

sentences.zh: 虎忽棄泰於地，走不顧，如人疾驅狀。

translations.literal: The tiger suddenly dropped Tai on the ground and ran off without looking back, as though a man were galloping away in haste.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger suddenly dropped Tai on the ground and fled without looking back, as if a man were racing away in panic.

sentences.zh: 泰匍匐而歸。

translations.literal: Tai crawled home on hands and knees.
translations.idiomatic: Tai crawled home on hands and knees.

sentences.zh: 母扶持以泣，泰亦強舉動，不逾月如故。

translations.literal: His mother supported him, weeping. Tai also forced himself to move about, and within a month he was as before.
translations.idiomatic: His mother supported him, weeping. Tai also forced himself to move about, and within a month he had recovered as before.

sentences.zh: 鄉里聞其孝感，率金帛遺之，里人目為朱虎殘。

translations.literal: When the village heard of his filial responsiveness, they all brought gold and silk as gifts. The villagers called him Zhu Tiger-Wounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the village heard of his filial devotion, neighbors brought him gold and silk. The locals called him Zhu, the One the Tiger Wounded.

sentences.zh: 成象，渠州流江人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xiang was a man of Liujiang in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xiang was a native of Liujiang in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 以詩書訓授里中，事父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He instructed the village in poetry and the classics, and was known for serving his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He taught poetry and the classics in his village and was known for filial service to his parents.

sentences.zh: 母病，割股肉食之，詔賜束帛醪酒。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her. An edict granted him silk rolls and libation wine.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her. The court issued an edict granting him silk rolls and libation wine.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，李順盜據郡縣，象父母驚悸而死，燼骨寄浮圖舍，象號泣營葬。

translations.literal: During Chunhua, Li Shun seized the prefectures and counties as a bandit. Xiang's parents died from fright and shock. Their burned bones were placed in a Buddhist monastery, and Xiang wailed and wept while arranging their burial.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, the rebel Li Shun seized the prefectures and counties. Xiang's parents died of shock and fright. Their charred bones were kept in a Buddhist monastery while Xiang wailed and arranged their burial.

sentences.zh: 賊平，鄉里率錢三百萬贈之。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the village collectively contributed three million cash as a gift to him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, the village collectively gave him three million cash.

sentences.zh: 象廬於墓側，以衰服襟袂篩土於墳上，日三斗。

translations.literal: Xiang built a hut beside the tomb. With the sleeves of his mourning garments he sifted earth onto the grave—three pecks a day.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang built a mourning hut beside the tomb and sifted earth onto the grave with the sleeves of his mourning robes—three pecks each day.

sentences.zh: 每慟，聞者戚愴。

translations.literal: Whenever he wailed in grief, those who heard him were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wailed in grief, those who heard him were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 未嘗食肉衣帛，或贈之亦不受。

translations.literal: He never ate meat or wore silk. Even when gifts were offered, he would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He never ate meat or wore silk, and even when such things were offered to him he refused them.

sentences.zh: 虎豹環廬而臥，象無畏色。

translations.literal: Tigers and leopards lay in a ring around his hut, yet Xiang showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers and leopards lay in a ring around his hut, yet Xiang showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 燕百餘集廬中，禾生墓側吐九穗。

translations.literal: More than a hundred swallows gathered in his hut, and millet grew beside the tomb bearing nine ears.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred swallows gathered in his hut, and millet sprang up beside the tomb with nine ears on each stalk.

sentences.zh: 服終猶未還家，知禮者為書以諭之，遂歸教授，遠近目為成孝子。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he still had not returned home. Men versed in ritual wrote to instruct him, and he then returned home to teach. Near and far people regarded him as Filial Son Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he still had not returned home. Men versed in ritual wrote to counsel him, and he then went home to teach again. People near and far called him Filial Son Cheng.

sentences.zh: 方綱，池州青陽人。

translations.literal: Fang Gang was a man of Qingyang in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Gang was a native of Qingyang in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 八世同爨，家屬七百口，居室六百區，每旦鳴鼓會食。

translations.literal: Eight generations shared one cooking fire. The household numbered seven hundred mouths, with six hundred dwelling units. Each morning a drum was sounded to assemble for meals.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations cooked at a single hearth. The household numbered seven hundred members in six hundred dwellings, and each morning a drum was beaten to call everyone to eat together.

sentences.zh: 嘗出稻五千{易}振貸貧民。

translations.literal: He once distributed five thousand shi of rice to relieve and lend to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He once distributed five thousand shi of rice to relieve and lend to the poor.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，轉運使馮亮以聞，詔旌其門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, Transport Commissioner Feng Liang reported the matter, and an edict honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde, Transport Commissioner Feng Liang reported the matter to the throne, and an edict honored his household gate.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，侍御史韓億安撫江南，使還，言綱家稅籍錢四百餘千，米二千五百斛，同居四百年，而本縣科率一無寬假，望蠲其戶雜科，詔從之。

translations.literal: During Tianxi, Censor Han Yi pacified Jiangnan. When he returned from his mission he reported that Gang's household tax register showed more than four hundred thousand cash and twenty-five hundred hu of grain; they had lived together for four hundred years, yet the home county granted not one exemption in levies. He requested remission of miscellaneous taxes for the household, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi era, Censor Han Yi was sent to pacify Jiangnan. On his return he reported that Gang's household was registered for more than four hundred thousand cash in taxes and twenty-five hundred hu of grain, and that the family had lived together for four hundred years, yet the home county had granted not a single exemption. He asked that miscellaneous levies on the household be remitted, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 龐天祐，江陵人。

translations.literal: Pang Tianyou was a man of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tianyou was a native of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 以經籍教授里中。

translations.literal: He instructed the village in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the classics in his village.

sentences.zh: 父疾，天祐割股肉食之；

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, Tianyou cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to him;
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, Tianyou cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to him;

sentences.zh: 疾愈，又復病目喪明，天祐號泣祈天舐之。

translations.literal: When the illness cleared, his father again fell ill in the eyes and lost his sight. Tianyou wailed, prayed to Heaven, and licked his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness cleared, his father again fell ill in the eyes and went blind. Tianyou wailed, prayed to Heaven, and licked his eyes.

sentences.zh: 父年八十餘，大中祥符四年卒，天祐負土封墳，結廬其側，晝夜號不絕聲。

translations.literal: His father was over eighty. In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died. Tianyou carried earth to seal the grave, built a hut beside it, and wailed day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: His father was over eighty. In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died. Tianyou carried earth to seal the grave, built a mourning hut beside it, and wailed day and night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 知府陳堯谘親往致奠，上其事，詔旌表門閭。

translations.literal: Prefect Chen Yaozi personally went to offer sacrifices, reported the matter upward, and an edict honored his gate and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Chen Yaozi went in person to offer sacrifices, reported the matter to the throne, and an edict honored his gate and neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 天祐家無儋石儲，居委巷中，堯谘為徙裏門之右，築闕表之。

translations.literal: Tianyou's family had no stores of even a dan and a shi of grain. He lived in a narrow lane. Yaozi had him moved to the right of the district gate and built a memorial arch to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou's family had scarcely a dan or shi of grain in store and lived in a narrow lane. Yaozi had him moved to the right side of the district gate and built a memorial arch to mark the honor.

sentences.zh: 劉斌，定州人。

translations.literal: Liu Bin was a man of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin was a native of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父加友，端拱中為從弟志元所殺。

translations.literal: His father Jiayou was killed in the Duangong era by his younger cousin Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiayou was killed in the Duangong era by his younger cousin Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 斌兄弟皆幼，隨母改適人，母嘗戒之曰：「爾等長，必復父仇。」

translations.literal: Bin and his brothers were all young and followed their mother when she remarried. Their mother once warned them, "When you grow up, you must avenge your father's death."
translations.idiomatic: Bin and his brothers were still young when their mother remarried and they went with her. She once warned them, "When you grow up, you must avenge your father's death."

sentences.zh: 景德中，斌兄弟挾刀伺志元於道，刺之不殊，即詣吏自陳。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, Bin and his brothers took knives and waited for Zhiyuan on the road. They stabbed him but did not kill him, then went straight to the officials and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era, Bin and his brothers took knives and lay in wait for Zhiyuan on the road. They stabbed him but did not kill him, then went straight to the magistrates and confessed.

sentences.zh: 州具獄上請，詔志元黥麵配隸汝州，釋斌等罪。

translations.literal: The prefecture compiled the case and submitted it for decision. An edict ordered Zhiyuan tattooed on the face and assigned as a bonded servant in Ruzhou, and released Bin and the others from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture compiled the case and submitted it for imperial decision. An edict ordered Zhiyuan tattooed on the face and assigned as a bonded servant in Ruzhou, and released Bin and his brothers from punishment.

sentences.zh: 樊景溫，陝州芮城人；

translations.literal: Fan Jingwen was a man of Ruicheng in Shanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen was a native of Ruicheng in Shanzhou;

sentences.zh: 榮恕旻，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Rong Shumin was a man of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Shumin was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄弟異居積年。

translations.literal: The brothers had lived separately for many years.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers had lived apart for many years.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，景溫樗樹五枝並為一，恕旻家榆樹兩本自合，兩家感其異，復義聚，鄉人稱雍睦。

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu, five branches of Jingwen's chinaberry tree merged into one, and two elms at Shumin's home joined of themselves. Both families were moved by the wonder and reunited in righteous community. The village called them harmonious and affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, five branches of Jingwen's chinaberry tree merged into one, and two elms at Shumin's home joined of their own accord. Both families were moved by the omen and reunited under one roof. The villagers called them a model of harmony.

sentences.zh: 祁暐字坦之，萊州膠水人。

translations.literal: Qi Wei, styled Tanzhi, was a man of Jiaoshui in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wei, whose courtesy name was Tanzhi, was a native of Jiaoshui in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年進士，曆度支員外郎、直集賢院。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Chunhua, he served successively as Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue and as a direct appointee to the Hall of Assembled Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Chunhua and served successively as Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue and as a direct appointee to the Hall of Assembled Eminence.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，出知濰州，母卒。

translations.literal: During Tianxi he was dispatched as prefect of Weizhou. His mother died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi era he was appointed prefect of Weizhou. His mother died.

sentences.zh: 葬於州城之南。

translations.literal: She was buried south of the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried south of the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 暐既解官，就墳側構小室，號泣守護，蔬食，經六冬，墮足二指。

translations.literal: Wei then resigned office, built a small room beside the grave, wailed and kept guard, ate only vegetables, and over six winters lost two toes to frostbite.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then resigned from office, built a small room beside the grave, and wailed as he kept watch, eating only vegetables. Over six winters he lost two toes to frostbite.

sentences.zh: 有白烏白兔馴擾墳側，州人異之，以狀聞。

translations.literal: A white crow and a white rabbit tamely lingered beside the grave. People in the prefecture marveled at it and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A white crow and a white rabbit tamely lingered beside the grave. People in the prefecture marveled at the omen and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 有詔旌美，賜帛三十匹、粟三十石，令長吏每月存問。

translations.literal: An edict praised him, granted thirty bolts of silk and thirty shi of grain, and ordered the chief officials to visit him monthly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his conduct, granted thirty bolts of silk and thirty shi of grain, and ordered the chief local officials to visit him each month.

sentences.zh: 何保之，梓州通泉人。

translations.literal: He Baozhi was a man of Tongquan in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Baozhi was a native of Tongquan in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 業進士，有至行。

translations.literal: He pursued the jinshi degree and possessed supreme conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the jinshi degree and was known for exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 母卒，負土成墳，廬於其側。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to build the grave and built a hut beside it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he carried earth to build the grave and erected a mourning hut beside it.

sentences.zh: 日有群烏飛集墳上，哀鳴不去，又嘗有兔馴於坐隅，人稱異焉。

translations.literal: Each day flocks of crows gathered on the grave, wailing mournfully and not leaving. A rabbit also once grew tame in the corner of his seat. People called it a marvel.
translations.idiomatic: Each day flocks of crows gathered on the grave, wailing mournfully and refusing to leave. A rabbit also once grew tame in the corner where he sat. People called these marvels.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符降詔旌恤。

translations.literal: In Dazhong Xiangfu an edict was issued to honor and console him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era an edict was issued to honor and console him.

sentences.zh: 李玭，大名宗城人。

translations.literal: Li Pin was a man of Zongcheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pin was a native of Zongcheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 性篤孝，力耕以事母。

translations.literal: By nature deeply filial, he farmed with his own strength to serve his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he farmed with his own hands to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 母卒，讓田與其弟堅，遂廬於葬所，晝夜號泣，負土築墳高丈餘。

translations.literal: When his mother died he yielded his fields to his younger brother Jian, then built a hut at the burial place, wailing day and night and carrying earth to build a grave more than a zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he gave his fields to his younger brother Jian, built a hut at the burial site, and wailed day and night as he carried earth to raise a grave more than ten feet high.

sentences.zh: 又以二代及諸族父母槁葬者盡禮築之，凡三年成六墳，皆丈餘。

translations.literal: He also properly built graves for parents of two generations and of the clan who had been given dry burial, completing six graves in three years, each over a zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave proper burial mounds to parents of two generations and to clan members who had received only dry burial, completing six graves over three years, each more than ten feet high.

sentences.zh: 不食肉衣帛，不預人事，遑遑然唯恐築之不及，墳成，復留守墳三年。

translations.literal: He ate no meat or silk, took no part in human affairs, and anxiously feared he could not finish the building. When the graves were done, he remained to guard them for three more years.
translations.idiomatic: He ate no meat and wore no silk, took no part in worldly affairs, and anxiously feared he could not finish the work in time. When the graves were complete, he remained to guard them for three more years.

sentences.zh: 常令兄之子賣藥以自給。

translations.literal: He often had his elder brother's son sell medicine to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He often had his brother's son sell medicine to support him.

sentences.zh: 年六十餘，足未嘗入縣門。

translations.literal: Past sixty years of age, his feet had never entered the county gate.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty, his feet had never crossed the county gate.

sentences.zh: 鄉人目為「李孝子」。

translations.literal: The villagers called him "Filial Son Li."
translations.idiomatic: The villagers called him "Filial Son Li."

sentences.zh: 天禧中，知府張知白以狀聞，詔賜粟帛，令府縣安存之。

translations.literal: During Tianxi, Prefect Zhang Zhibai reported the matter, and an edict granted grain and silk and ordered the prefecture and county to provide for his comfort.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi era, Prefect Zhang Zhibai reported the matter to the throne. An edict granted grain and silk and ordered the prefecture and county to look after him.

sentences.zh: 里中有母在而析產者聞比被旌，兄弟慚懼，復相率同居。

translations.literal: In the village, brothers who had divided property while their mother still lived heard that Bi had been honored. Shamed and afraid, they again gathered to live together.
translations.idiomatic: In the village, brothers who had divided the family property while their mother was still alive heard that Bi had been honored. Ashamed and afraid, they gathered again to live together.

sentences.zh: 侯義，應天府楚丘人。

translations.literal: Hou Yi was a man of Chuqiu in Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi was a native of Chuqiu in Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貧無產，傭田以事母。

translations.literal: Poor and without property, he hired out to farm in order to serve his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and landless, he hired himself out to farm in order to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 里人有葬其親而遽返者，義母過其塚，泣謂義曰：「我死，其若是乎！」

translations.literal: A villager buried a relative and hurried back. Yi's mother passed the tomb and wept, saying to Yi, "When I die, will it be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor buried a relative and hurried back. Yi's mother passed the grave and wept, saying to him, "When I die, will it be like this?"

sentences.zh: 義乃感激自誓而不欲言，但慰其母曰：「勿悲，義必不爾。」

translations.literal: Yi was stirred and swore an oath to himself but did not wish to speak of it. He only comforted his mother, saying, "Do not grieve—I shall certainly not be like that."
translations.idiomatic: Yi was deeply moved and swore a private oath, but he did not wish to speak of it. He only comforted his mother, saying, "Do not grieve—I shall certainly not be like that."

sentences.zh: 咸平中，母卒，義力自辦葬，不掩墳壙，晝則負土築墳，夜則慟哭柩側。

translations.literal: In Xianping his mother died. Yi strained to arrange the burial himself and did not seal the grave chamber. By day he carried earth to build the mound; by night he wailed beside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era his mother died. Yi strained to arrange the burial himself and did not seal the grave chamber. By day he carried earth to build the mound; by night he wailed beside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 妻子困匱不給，田主曹氏哀憐之，資以餱糧。

translations.literal: His wife and children were destitute and could not get by. The landowner, the Cao family, pitied him and supplied him with dry provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were destitute and could not make ends meet. The landowner, the Cao family, took pity on him and supplied him with dry provisions.

sentences.zh: 逾年，墳間瓜異蒂、木連理，又有巨蛇繞其側不暴物，野鴿飛而不去。

translations.literal: After more than a year, melons at the grave bore fruit on shared stems and trees grew conjoined. A great serpent also coiled beside the site without harming anything, and wild pigeons flew there but did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, melons at the grave bore fruit on shared stems and trees grew conjoined. A great serpent also coiled beside the site without harming anything, and wild pigeons flew there but would not leave.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇盜劫其衣服，既而知是義物，悉還之。

translations.literal: Robbers once seized his clothes, but when they learned they belonged to Yi they returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers once seized his clothes, but when they learned they belonged to Yi they returned them all.

sentences.zh: 王光濟，廬州人。

translations.literal: Wang Guangji was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangji was a native of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪母，因刻像日夕奉事如平生，孝道純篤。

translations.literal: After his mother's death he carved her image and waited on it morning and evening as in life. His filial devotion was pure and deep.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he carved her image and waited on it morning and evening as though she were still alive. His filial devotion was pure and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，本州以孝聞，有詔旌之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping the prefecture reported his filial piety, and an edict honored him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping the prefecture reported his filial piety to the throne, and an edict honored him.

sentences.zh: 時又有徐州豐人李祚，親喪，廬墓側凡二十七年，家人百計勉諭，不聽。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Li Zuo of Feng in Xuzhou. After a parent's death he dwelt beside the tomb for twenty-seven years. His family tried every means to encourage and instruct him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also Li Zuo of Feng in Xuzhou. After a parent's death he lived beside the tomb for twenty-seven years. His family tried every means to persuade him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 益州雙流人周善敏，喪父，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: Zhou Shanmin of Shuangliu in Yizhou mourned his father and built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shanmin of Shuangliu in Yizhou mourned his father and built a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 母病，又割股肉以啖之，遂愈。
