translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he again cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he again cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，特詔旌表祚，賜善敏粟帛存慰之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, a special edict honored Zuo, and granted Shanmin grain and silk in consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, a special edict honored Zuo, and granted Shanmin grain and silk as consolation.

sentences.zh: 江白，建昌人。

translations.literal: Jiang Bai was a man of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bai was a native of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 景德二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingde.

sentences.zh: 父禹錫，有節義，高年不仕，躬自教授，大中祥符初，獻《東封詩》十五篇，有詔嘉美，賜以粟帛，歲時遣使存問。

translations.literal: His father Yuxi possessed integrity and righteousness. In advanced years he did not take office and personally taught. At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he presented fifteen poems on the Eastern Sacrifice. An edict praised him, granted grain and silk, and dispatched envoys at regular seasons to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuxi was a man of integrity and moral courage. In his old age he did not take office and taught on his own. At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era he presented fifteen poems on the Eastern Sacrifice. An edict praised him, granted grain and silk, and sent envoys at the proper seasons to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died.

sentences.zh: 白自鄞尉罷還，負土營葬，廬於墓側，藜羹芒屩，晝夜號泣，將終製猶然。

translations.literal: Bai returned after leaving office as Assistant Magistrate of Yin. He carried earth to arrange the burial, built a hut beside the grave, ate wild vegetable broth and wore straw sandals, and wailed day and night—still so even as mourning neared its end.
translations.idiomatic: Bai returned after leaving his post as Assistant Magistrate of Yin. He carried earth to arrange the burial, built a hut beside the grave, ate wild vegetable broth and wore straw sandals, and wailed day and night—even as mourning neared its end.

sentences.zh: 轉運使以其狀聞，詔賜帛二十匹，粟麥二十石，醪酒十缸。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported his condition. An edict granted twenty bolts of silk, twenty shi of grain and wheat, and ten jars of libation wine.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner reported his condition to the throne. An edict granted twenty bolts of silk, twenty shi of grain and wheat, and ten jars of libation wine.

sentences.zh: 裘承詢，越州會稽人。

translations.literal: Qiu Chengxun was a man of Kuaiji in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Chengxun was a native of Kuaiji in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 居雲門山前，十九世無異爨。

translations.literal: He lived before Yunmen Mountain. Nineteen generations shared one cooking fire without separate kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: The family lived below Yunmen Mountain. For nineteen generations they shared a single hearth without separate kitchens.

sentences.zh: 子弟習弦誦，鄉里稱其敦睦。

translations.literal: Sons and nephews studied the classics, and the village praised their warmth and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and nephews studied the classics, and the village praised their warmth and harmony.

sentences.zh: 州以聞，詔旌其門閭。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported it, and an edict honored their gate and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported the matter, and an edict honored their gate and neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 咸平後，又有保定軍孫浦、襄州常元紹、蔡州王美、解州董孝章並十世同居；

translations.literal: After Xianping, there were also Sun Pu of Baoding Army, Chang Yuanshao of Xiangzhou, Wang Mei of Caizhou, and Dong Xiaozhang of Jiezhou—all living together for ten generations;
translations.idiomatic: After the Xianping era there were also Sun Pu of Baoding Army, Chang Yuanshao of Xiangzhou, Wang Mei of Caizhou, and Dong Xiaozhang of Jiezhou—all of whom had lived together for ten generations;

sentences.zh: 莫州高珪、永定軍朱仁貴、潞州邢濬、相州趙祚八世同居；

translations.literal: Gao Gui of Mozhou, Zhu Rengui of Yongding Army, Xing Jun of Luzhou, and Zhao Zuo of Xiangzhou—eight generations living together;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gui of Mozhou, Zhu Rengui of Yongding Army, Xing Jun of Luzhou, and Zhao Zuo of Xiangzhou—eight generations living together;

sentences.zh: 麟州楊榮、隰州趙友、開封李居正、潁州張可象、衛州張珪、滄州崔諒七世同居；

translations.literal: Yang Rong of Linzhou, Zhao You of Xizhou, Li Juzheng of Kaifeng, Zhang Kexiang of Yingzhou, Zhang Gui of Weizhou, and Cui Liang of Cangzhou—seven generations living together;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong of Linzhou, Zhao You of Xizhou, Li Juzheng of Kaifeng, Zhang Kexiang of Yingzhou, Zhang Gui of Weizhou, and Cui Liang of Cangzhou—seven generations living together;

sentences.zh: 邢州王覺、趙州曹遵六世同居；

translations.literal: Wang Jue of Xingzhou and Cao Zun of Zhaozhou—six generations living together;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jue of Xingzhou and Cao Zun of Zhaozhou—six generations living together;

sentences.zh: 兗州童升、陳州樊可行、京兆元守全、平定軍段德五世同居；

translations.literal: Tong Sheng of Yanzhou, Fan Kexing of Chenzhou, Yuan Shouquan of Jingzhao, and Duan De of Pingding Army—five generations living together;
translations.idiomatic: Tong Sheng of Yanzhou, Fan Kexing of Chenzhou, Yuan Shouquan of Jingzhao, and Duan De of Pingding Army—five generations living together;

sentences.zh: 開封張仁遇、亳州王子上、建昌軍瞿肅四世同居。

translations.literal: Zhang Renyu of Kaifeng, Wang Wangzi of Bozhou, and Qu Su of Jianchang Army—four generations living together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyu of Kaifeng, Wang Wangzi of Bozhou, and Qu Su of Jianchang Army—four generations living together.

sentences.zh: 肅家百五十口，長幼孝悌，鄉人化之。

translations.literal: Su's household numbered one hundred fifty mouths. Young and old were filial and fraternal, and the village was transformed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Su's household numbered one hundred fifty members. Young and old were filial and fraternal, and the village was transformed by their example.

sentences.zh: 又河陰王世及、大名李宗祐、陳州劉閏、宣州汪政、潭州李耕，或聚居至七百口，累數十百年。

translations.literal: Also Wang Shiji of Heyin, Li Zongyou of Daming, Liu Run of Chenzhou, Wang Zheng of Xuanzhou, and Li Geng of Tanzhou—some gathered in communities of up to seven hundred mouths, continuing for decades and centuries.
translations.idiomatic: Also Wang Shiji of Heyin, Li Zongyou of Daming, Liu Run of Chenzhou, Wang Zheng of Xuanzhou, and Li Geng of Tanzhou—some of whose households gathered as many as seven hundred members and had lived together for decades and centuries.

sentences.zh: 並所在請加旌表，詔從之，仍蠲其課調。

translations.literal: In each locality they requested additional honors, and an edict approved, remitting their tax levies as well.
translations.idiomatic: In each locality they requested further honors, and an edict approved, remitting their tax levies as well.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，東封泰山，判兗州王欽若言曲阜東野宜、乾封竇益合居五六世，有節行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the Eastern Sacrifice was performed at Mount Tai, Wang Qinruo, acting prefect of Yanzhou, reported that Dong Yiyi of Qufu and Dou Yi of Qianfeng had lived together for five or six generations with upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when the Eastern Sacrifice was performed at Mount Tai, Wang Qinruo, acting prefect of Yanzhou, reported that Dong Yiyi of Qufu and Dou Yi of Qianfeng had lived together for five or six generations and were known for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 四年，祀汾陰，考制度使馬起言陝州張化基、閻用和、楊忠義聚族累世，孝悌可稱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the sacrifice was performed at Fenyin, Commissioner for Examining Rites Ma Qi reported that Zhang Huaji, Yan Yonghe, and Yang Zhongyi of Shanzhou had gathered their clans for successive generations, their filial piety and brotherly respect worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the sacrifice was performed at Fenyin, Commissioner for Examining Rites Ma Qi reported that Zhang Huaji, Yan Yonghe, and Yang Zhongyi of Shanzhou had gathered their clans for successive generations, and that their filial piety and brotherly devotion were worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 並即行在所降詔褒美，各優賜粟帛。

translations.literal: Edicts of commendation were immediately issued from the traveling palace, and each was specially granted grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts of commendation were immediately issued from the imperial procession, and each was specially granted grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 常真，陳州項城人。

translations.literal: Chang Zhen was a man of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhen was a native of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父母死，廬墓終喪，負土成墳，不茹葷血。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he built a hut at the grave and completed mourning, carrying earth on his back to form the mound. He ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he built a mourning hut at their grave and completed the mourning period, carrying earth on his back to build the mound. He ate no meat.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，詔旌其門閭。

translations.literal: During Later Zhou's Guangshun era, an edict marked his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, an edict honored his household.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，本州以聞，詔再加旌表。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao, the prefecture reported it, and an edict further honored his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaibao, the prefecture reported him to the throne, and an edict further honored his household.

sentences.zh: 真妻病，子晏割股肉以養母，及死，次子守規徒跣，日一食，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When Zhen's wife fell ill, his son Yan cut flesh from his thigh to nourish his mother. When she died, the second son Shougui went barefoot, ate one meal a day, and built a hut at the grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen's wife fell ill, his son Yan cut flesh from his thigh to nourish her. When she died, the second son Shougui went barefoot, ate one meal a day, and lived in a hut beside the grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，詔旌表之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict honored them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict honored their household.

sentences.zh: 又有齊州王洤、河南李繼成、滄州胡元興，並母死負土成墳，晝夜哭不絕聲。

translations.literal: There were also Wang Ping of Qizhou, Li Jicheng of Henan, and Hu Yuanxing of Cangzhou—all after their mothers' deaths carried earth to form graves and wept day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Wang Ping of Qizhou, Li Jicheng of Henan, and Hu Yuanxing of Cangzhou—all of whom, after their mothers died, carried earth on their backs to build graves and wept day and night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 州郡繼以聞，皆降詔旌其門閭，賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: The prefectures successively reported this. Edicts were issued in each case to mark their household gates, and grain and cloth were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures successively reported them to the throne. In each case edicts were issued to honor their households, and they were granted grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 杜誼字漢臣，台州黃岩人。

translations.literal: Du Yi, courtesy name Hanchen, was a man of Huangyan in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Huangyan in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 事父母至孝。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was supremely filial in serving his parents.

sentences.zh: 父剛嚴，誼獨失愛，惴惴不自容，伺顏色而後進。

translations.literal: His father was stern and severe. Yi alone did not enjoy his favor and was fearful and ill at ease, watching his expression before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: His father was stern and severe. Yi alone did not enjoy his favor and lived in constant fear, watching his father's expression before daring to approach.

sentences.zh: 繼喪父母，號慟晝夜不絕，勺水不入口者累日。

translations.literal: After the successive deaths of his parents, he wailed day and night without cease and for many days would not take even a spoonful of water into his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: After burying both parents in succession, he wailed day and night without stopping and for many days refused even a spoonful of water.

sentences.zh: 卜葬，徒跣負土為墳，往來十餘里，日渡塘澗，泥水沒骭，雖大雨雪未嘗少止。

translations.literal: When he chose a burial site, he went barefoot and carried earth on his back to build the grave, traveling back and forth over ten li each day, crossing ponds and brooks with mud and water reaching his shins. Even in heavy rain and snow he never stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he chose a burial site, he went barefoot and carried earth on his back to build the grave, making daily trips of more than ten li and crossing ponds and brooks with mud and water up to his shins. Even in driving rain and snow he never slackened.

sentences.zh: 手足皸裂血流，以漆塗之。

translations.literal: His hands and feet cracked and bled; he applied lacquer to them.
translations.idiomatic: His hands and feet cracked and bled, and he treated them with lacquer.

sentences.zh: 每覆一畚，必三繞墳號而後去。

translations.literal: Each time he spread one basketload, he would circle the grave wailing three times before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he deposited one basketload of earth, he would circle the grave wailing three times before departing.

sentences.zh: 既葬，遂茇舍墓旁，負土終喪，人往視之，輒遣去。

translations.literal: After the burial he built a thatched hut beside the grave and carried earth until mourning was complete. When people came to see him he always sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he built a thatched hut beside the grave and carried earth until mourning was complete. Whenever people came to visit, he sent them away.

sentences.zh: 日一飯，不葷。

translations.literal: He ate one meal a day and took no meat.
translations.idiomatic: He ate one meal a day and abstained from meat.

sentences.zh: 雖虎狼交於墓側，誼泰然無所畏。

translations.literal: Although tigers and wolves wandered about beside the grave, Yi was calm and unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: Although tigers and wolves prowled beside the grave, Yi remained calm and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 明年，吳越大水，山皆發洚，推巨石走十數里。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great flood in Wu-Yue. Mountains all burst into torrents, hurling boulders ten-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a great flood struck Wu-Yue. Mountains burst into torrents that sent boulders rolling for miles.

sentences.zh: 台州山最高而水又夜至，旁山之民，居廬、墓田、畜牧漂壞者甚眾，而獨不及誼。

translations.literal: Taizhou's mountains were the highest and the water came by night as well. Among the people on nearby mountains, very many lost their dwellings, grave plots, fields, and livestock to the flood, but Yi alone was untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou's mountains were the highest, and the flood came by night as well. Among the people on neighboring peaks, very many lost their dwellings, burial plots, fields, and livestock—yet Yi alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 邑人狀其事以聞，詔書嘉獎。

translations.literal: The townspeople submitted a petition reporting the matter, and an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople submitted a petition to report the matter, and an imperial edict praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 事族父衍甚謹，衍愛之均諸子。

translations.literal: In serving his clansman uncle Yan he was exceedingly respectful. Yan loved him as he did his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He served his uncle Yan, a clansman, with great respect, and Yan loved him as he did his own sons.

sentences.zh: 以祖垂象蔭入官，至讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Through the yin privilege of his grandfather Chuixiang he entered office, rising to Attendant Gentleman for Moral Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Through the yin privilege of his grandfather Chuixiang he entered official service and rose to Attendant Gentleman for Moral Instruction.

sentences.zh: 嘗知永城縣，歲捐奉錢三十萬，以收瘞汴渠之溺死者凡四十餘。

translations.literal: He once served as magistrate of Yongcheng County. Each year he donated three hundred thousand cash from his salary to retrieve and bury the drowned in the Bian Canal—more than forty in all.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as magistrate of Yongcheng County. Each year he donated three hundred thousand cash from his salary to recover and bury the drowned in the Bian Canal—more than forty in all.

sentences.zh: 又出奉錢率其下新文宣王廟，兩旁為學舍數十區，旦夕講學於其堂。

translations.literal: He also paid from his salary to lead his subordinates in rebuilding the Temple of the Cultural Sage, with several tens of schoolrooms on both sides, and lectured there morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He also used his salary to lead his subordinates in rebuilding the Temple of the Cultural Sage, erecting several dozen schoolrooms on both sides and lecturing there morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 永城父老稱誼之政為不可及。

translations.literal: The elders of Yongcheng said that Yi's governance was beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Yongcheng said that Yi's governance was beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 誼生平敦厚，尚信義，有大志，家貧，不恤有無，常推以濟親友。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature sincere and generous, valued faith and righteousness, and had great aspiration. Though poor at home, he cared nothing for having or lacking and often gave away what he could to help kinsmen and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was sincere and generous by nature, valued faith and righteousness, and harbored great ambition. Though his family was poor, he gave little thought to his own wants and often shared what he had to help kinsmen and friends.

sentences.zh: 後通判梓州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as vice prefect of Zizhou, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice prefect of Zizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子揆才十六歲，哭誼墓旁卒。

translations.literal: His son Kui was only sixteen. He died weeping beside Yi's grave.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui was only sixteen when he died weeping beside Yi's grave.

sentences.zh: 姚宗明，河中永樂人也。

translations.literal: Yao Zongming was a man of Yongle in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zongming was a native of Yongle in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 其十世祖棲雲。

translations.literal: His tenth-generation ancestor was Qiyun.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-generation ancestor was Qiyun.

sentences.zh: 當唐貞元中，調卒戍邊，棲雲之父語其兄曰：「兄嗣未立，可無往。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era of Tang, when conscript laborers were dispatched to garrison the frontier, Qiyun's father said to his elder brother: "Your line of succession is not yet established. You need not go.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era of Tang, when conscripts were summoned to garrison the frontier, Qiyun's father said to his elder brother, "Your succession is not yet secured. You need not go.

sentences.zh: 某幸有子，請代兄行。」

translations.literal: I am fortunate to have a son. I ask to go in my brother's place."
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate to have a son. Please let me go in your place."

sentences.zh: 遂戰沒塞上。

translations.literal: He then fell in battle at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell in battle on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時棲雲方三歲，其母再嫁，棲雲養於伯母。

translations.literal: At that time Qiyun was only three. His mother remarried, and Qiyun was raised by his aunt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qiyun was only three years old. His mother remarried, and Qiyun was raised by his aunt.

sentences.zh: 既長，事伯母如其母，伯母亡，棲雲葬之。

translations.literal: When he grew up he served his aunt as his own mother. When his aunt died, Qiyun buried her.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he served his aunt as though she were his own mother. When she died, Qiyun buried her.

sentences.zh: 又招魂葬其父，痛其父死於邊，乃廬於墓次，終身哀慕不衰。

translations.literal: He also performed a soul-summoning burial for his father. Grieving that his father had died on the frontier, he built a hut beside the grave and maintained mourning and longing all his life without decline.
translations.idiomatic: He also performed a soul-summoning burial for his father. Deeply grieved that his father had died on the frontier, he built a hut beside the grave and remained in mourning and longing for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 縣令蘇轍以俸錢買地，開阡刻石表之。

translations.literal: The county magistrate Su Zhe used his salary to buy land, open a burial path, and carve stone to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate Su Zhe used his salary to buy land, open a burial path, and erect a stone marker.

sentences.zh: 河中尹渾瑊上其事，詔加優賜，表其門，名其鄉曰孝悌，社曰節義，裏曰敬愛。

translations.literal: Hezhong Prefect Hun Zhen memorialized the matter. An edict granted additional favors, marked his gate, and named his village Xiaoti, his community Jieyi, and his hamlet Jingai.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong Prefect Hun Zhen memorialized the matter. An edict granted additional rewards, honored his household gate, and named his village Filial and Fraternal, his community Integrity and Righteousness, and his hamlet Reverence and Love.

sentences.zh: 棲雲生嶽，嶽生君儒，君儒生師正。

translations.literal: Qiyun begot Yue; Yue begot Junru; Junru begot Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun begot Yue; Yue begot Junru; and Junru begot Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 自嶽至師正，四世廬墓。

translations.literal: From Yue to Shizheng, four generations built huts at graves.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue to Shizheng, four generations lived in mourning huts beside the graves.

sentences.zh: 五世孫曰厚，六世曰雅，七世曰文，八世曰敬真，九世曰直，十世曰宗明。

translations.literal: The fifth-generation descendant was called Hou; the sixth, Ya; the seventh, Wen; the eighth, Jingzhen; the ninth, Zhi; the tenth, Zongming.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth-generation descendant was Hou; the sixth was Ya; the seventh was Wen; the eighth was Jingzhen; the ninth was Zhi; and the tenth was Zongming.

sentences.zh: 當慶曆初，有司以姚氏十世同居聞於朝，仁宗詔復其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, the authorities reported that the Yao clan had lived together for ten generations. Emperor Renzong issued an edict remitting their tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingli era, officials reported to the court that the Yao clan had lived together for ten generations. Emperor Renzong issued an edict remitting their household tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 十一世孫用和，十二世孫士明，十三世孫德。

translations.literal: The eleventh-generation descendant was Yonghe; the twelfth, Shiming; the thirteenth, De.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh-generation descendant was Yonghe; the twelfth was Shiming; and the thirteenth was De.

sentences.zh: 自宗明至德又三世，自慶曆以後又五十餘年，而其家孝睦不替。

translations.literal: From Zongming to De was another three generations; more than fifty years had passed since Qingli, yet the household's filial harmony did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: From Zongming to De covered another three generations; more than fifty years had passed since the Qingli era, yet the clan's filial harmony had not faded.

sentences.zh: 姚氏世為農，無為學者。

translations.literal: The Yao clan for generations were farmers; none became scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao clan were farmers for generations; none became scholars.

sentences.zh: 家不甚富，有田數十頃，聚族百餘人。

translations.literal: The family was not very wealthy. They had several tens of qing of land and gathered more than a hundred clan members.
translations.idiomatic: The family was not very wealthy. They held several dozen qing of land and numbered more than a hundred clan members living together.

sentences.zh: 子孫躬事農桑，僅給衣食，曆三百餘年無異辭者。

translations.literal: The descendants personally worked farming and sericulture, barely supplying food and clothing. For more than three hundred years none among them had dissenting words.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants personally worked the fields and tended the silkworms, barely supplying their own food and clothing. For more than three hundred years none among them had ever quarreled.

sentences.zh: 經唐末、五代，兵戈亂離，而子孫保守墳墓，骨肉不相離散，求之天下，未或有焉。

translations.literal: Through the end of Tang and the Five Dynasties, amid warfare and turmoil, the descendants preserved the graves and kin did not scatter. Searched for throughout the empire, perhaps nowhere was there such a case.
translations.idiomatic: Through the end of Tang and the Five Dynasties, amid warfare and turmoil, the descendants preserved the graves and kin did not scatter. Searched for throughout the empire, perhaps nowhere else was there such a case.

sentences.zh: 鄧中和字祖德，開封長垣人。

translations.literal: Deng Zhonghe, courtesy name Zude, was a man of Changyuan in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhonghe, courtesy name Zude, was a native of Changyuan in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 舉《三禮》。

translations.literal: He passed the Three Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 景祐、慶曆間喪親，廬墓終其喪，定省往來如事生者二十年，負土累墳高三丈。

translations.literal: Between Jingyou and Qingli he mourned his parents, built a hut at the grave and completed mourning, attending morning and evening as though they lived—for twenty years—and carried earth to raise the mound three zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jingyou and Qingli eras he mourned his parents, lived in a hut beside the grave through the full mourning period, and for twenty years attended the site morning and evening as though they were still alive, carrying earth until the mound stood three zhang high.

sentences.zh: 毛安輿，嘉州洪雅人。

translations.literal: Mao Anyu was a man of Hongya in Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Anyu was a native of Hongya in Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 年九歲父死，負土為墳，廬於其側三年。

translations.literal: When he was nine his father died. He carried earth to build the grave and built a hut beside it for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine his father died. He carried earth on his back to build the grave and lived in a hut beside it for three years.

sentences.zh: 知益州張方平聞之，遺以酒餼，狀其事以聞。

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping, prefect of Yizhou, heard of this, sent him wine and food, and submitted a memorial reporting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping, prefect of Yizhou, heard of this, sent him wine and food gifts, and submitted a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李訪，韶州人，業進士。

translations.literal: Li Fang was a man of Shaozhou and pursued the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang was a native of Shaozhou and pursued the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 廬父母墓，有虎暴傷旁人而不近訪，又有白烏集墓上。

translations.literal: He built a hut at his parents' grave. A tiger ravaged the area and injured others but would not approach Fang. White crows also gathered atop the grave.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside his parents' grave. A tiger ravaged the area and injured others but would not approach Fang. White crows also gathered atop the grave.

sentences.zh: 朱壽昌字康叔，揚州天長人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouchang, courtesy name Kangshu, was a man of Tianchang in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouchang, courtesy name Kangshu, was a native of Tianchang in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父巽蔭守將作監主簿，累調州縣，通判陝州、荊南，權知岳州。

translations.literal: Through the yin privilege of his father Sun he served as registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. After successive appointments in prefectures and counties, he served as vice prefect of Shaanzhou and Jingnan, and acting prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through the yin privilege of his father Sun he served as registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. After successive postings in prefectures and counties, he served as vice prefect of Shaanzhou and Jingnan, and as acting prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 州濱重湖，多水盜。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered a great lake and had many river pirates.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered a great lake and suffered from many river pirates.

sentences.zh: 壽昌籍民船，刻著名氏，使相伺察，出入必以告。

translations.literal: Shouchang registered civilian boats and carved names on them, making them keep watch on one another. Entry and exit had always to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang registered civilian boats and inscribed their owners' names, making them watch one another. Departures and arrivals had to be reported without fail.

sentences.zh: 盜發，驗船所向窮討之，盜為少弭，旁郡取以為法。

translations.literal: When theft occurred, he traced the direction of the boats and pursued investigation to the end. Banditry was somewhat curbed, and neighboring prefectures took this as a model.
translations.idiomatic: When theft occurred, he traced the boats' movements and pursued the culprits to the end. Piracy eased somewhat, and neighboring prefectures took his method as a model.

sentences.zh: 富弼、韓琦為相，遣使四出寬恤民力，擇壽昌使湖南。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi and Han Qi served as chief ministers, they dispatched envoys in all directions to lighten burdens on the people. Shouchang was chosen to serve Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi and Han Qi served as chief ministers, they dispatched envoys in all directions to lighten the people's burdens. Shouchang was chosen to serve as envoy to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 或言邵州可置冶采金者，有詔興作。

translations.literal: Someone proposed that Shaozhou could establish smelting works to mine gold. An edict ordered the project begun.
translations.idiomatic: Someone proposed establishing gold-smelting works in Shaozhou. An edict ordered construction to begin.

sentences.zh: 壽昌言州近蠻，金冶若大發，蠻必爭，自此邊境恐多事，且廢良田數百頃，非敦本抑末之道也。

translations.literal: Shouchang stated that the prefecture was near the barbarians; if gold smelting were greatly expanded the barbarians would surely contend for it, and from then on the frontier would likely see much trouble. Moreover, several hundred qing of good farmland would be abandoned—this was not the way of prioritizing fundamentals and restraining secondary pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang argued that the prefecture lay near tribal territories, that large-scale gold smelting would provoke conflict with the tribes and likely bring trouble to the frontier, and that several hundred qing of good farmland would be ruined—all contrary to the principle of nurturing the fundamental and restraining secondary pursuits.

sentences.zh: 詔亟罷之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately halted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately halted the project.

sentences.zh: 知閬州，大姓雍子良屢殺人，挾財與勢得不死。

translations.literal: As prefect of Langzhou, a great clan's scion Yong Ziliang repeatedly killed people. Relying on wealth and influence he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Langzhou, he confronted Yong Ziliang, a powerful clan member who had repeatedly killed people yet escaped death through wealth and influence.

sentences.zh: 至是，又殺人而賂其裏民出就吏。

translations.literal: On this occasion he again killed someone and bribed a man of his hamlet to turn himself in to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he again killed someone and bribed a man from his hamlet to surrender to the authorities in his stead.

sentences.zh: 獄具，壽昌覺其奸，引囚詰之曰：「吾聞子良與汝錢十萬，許納汝女為婦，且婿汝子，故汝代其命，有之乎？」

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Shouchang sensed the fraud. He brought the prisoner forward and interrogated him, saying: "I hear Ziliang gave you one hundred thousand cash, promising to take your daughter as wife and also betroth her to your son—that is why you take his death sentence. Is this so?"
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, Shouchang sensed the fraud. He brought the prisoner forward and questioned him: "I hear Ziliang gave you one hundred thousand cash, promising to take your daughter as wife and betroth her to your son—that is why you would die in his place. Is this true?"

sentences.zh: 囚色動，則又擿之曰：「汝且死，書券抑汝女為婢，指錢為顧直，又不婿汝子，將奈何？」

translations.literal: The prisoner's countenance changed. Shouchang pressed further: "You are about to die. The written contract demotes your daughter to maidservant and treats the money as hire-price, and he will not betroth her to your son—what then will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: The prisoner's face changed. Shouchang pressed further: "You are about to die. The written contract would reduce your daughter to a maidservant and treat the money as a hiring fee, and he will not betroth her to your son—what then?"

sentences.zh: 囚悟，泣涕覆麵，曰：「囚幾誤死。」

translations.literal: The prisoner came to understanding, wept with face covered, and said: "This prisoner nearly died in error."
translations.idiomatic: The prisoner understood, wept with his face covered, and said, "I nearly died for nothing."

sentences.zh: 以實對。

translations.literal: He answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: He told the full truth.

sentences.zh: 立取子良正諸法。

translations.literal: Shouchang immediately had Ziliang executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang immediately had Ziliang executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 郡稱為神，蜀人至今傳之。

translations.literal: The prefecture called him divine; people of Shu still tell the story to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture hailed him as miraculous, and people of Shu still tell the story to this day.

sentences.zh: 知廣德軍。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 壽昌母劉氏，巽妾也。

translations.literal: Shouchang's mother, Lady Liu, was a concubine of Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang's mother, Lady Liu, was a concubine of Sun.

sentences.zh: 巽守京兆，劉氏方娠而出。

translations.literal: When Sun served as prefect of Jingzhao, Lady Liu was pregnant when she was sent away.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun served as prefect of Jingzhao, Lady Liu had just become pregnant when she was sent away.

sentences.zh: 壽昌生數歲始歸父家，母子不相聞五十年。

translations.literal: Shouchang was several years old when he first returned to his father's household. Mother and son had no contact for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang was several years old when he first returned to his father's household. Mother and son had no contact for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 行四方求之不置，飲食罕禦酒肉，言輒流涕。

translations.literal: He traveled everywhere seeking her without cease. In food and drink he rarely allowed himself wine and meat, and whenever he spoke he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled everywhere searching for her without rest. He rarely touched wine or meat and wept whenever he spoke of her.

sentences.zh: 用浮屠法灼背燒頂，刺血書佛經，力所可致，無不為者。

translations.literal: Using Buddhist methods he burned his back and scorched his crown, pricked blood to copy sutras—whatever effort he could make, there was nothing he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Using Buddhist practices he burned his back and scorched his crown, pricked his finger to copy sutras in blood—there was nothing within his power that he did not try.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，與家人辭訣，棄官入秦，曰：「不見母，吾不反矣。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he bade farewell to his family, abandoned office, and entered Qin, saying: "If I do not see my mother, I shall not return."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era he bade farewell to his family, resigned his post, and entered Qin, saying, "If I do not find my mother, I shall not return."

sentences.zh: 遂得之於同州。

translations.literal: He then found her in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He found her in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉時年七十餘矣，嫁黨氏有數子，悉迎以歸。

translations.literal: Liu was then over seventy. She had married into the Dang clan and had several sons. Shouchang welcomed them all to return with him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was then over seventy. She had married into the Dang clan and borne several sons. Shouchang welcomed them all to return with him.

sentences.zh: 京兆錢明逸以其事聞，詔還就官，由是以孝聞天下。

translations.literal: Qian Mingyi of Jingzhao reported the matter. An edict ordered him to return and resume office, and from this his filial piety became known throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Mingyi of Jingzhao reported the matter to the throne. An edict ordered him to return and resume office, and from this his filial piety became known throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 自王安石、蘇頌、蘇軾以下，士大夫爭為詩美之。

translations.literal: From Wang Anshi, Su Song, and Su Shi on down, scholar-officials competed to compose poems praising him.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Anshi, Su Song, and Su Shi on down, scholar-officials competed to compose poems in his praise.

sentences.zh: 壽昌以養母故，求通判河中府。

translations.literal: Shouchang, to care for his mother, requested appointment as vice prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang, to care for his mother, requested appointment as vice prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數歲母卒，壽昌居喪幾喪明。

translations.literal: Several years later his mother died. Shouchang observed mourning and nearly lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his mother died. Shouchang observed mourning and nearly lost his sight.

sentences.zh: 既葬，有白烏集墓上。

translations.literal: After the burial, white crows gathered atop the grave.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, white crows gathered atop the grave.

sentences.zh: 拊同母弟妹益篤。

translations.literal: He was especially devoted in cherishing his younger siblings by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: He grew especially devoted to his younger half-siblings.

sentences.zh: 又知鄂州，提舉崇禧觀，累官司農少卿，易朝議大夫，遷中散大夫，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He again served as prefect of Ezhou, as commissioner of the Chongxi Abbey, rose through the offices of Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry of Agriculture, exchanged to Grandee for Discussion, was promoted to Grandee of Palace Attendance, and died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Ezhou and as commissioner of the Chongxi Abbey, rose through appointments including Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry of Agriculture, was given the rank of Grandee for Discussion, promoted to Grandee of Palace Attendance, and died at age seventy.

sentences.zh: 壽昌勇於義，周人之急無所愛，嫁兄弟兩孤女，葬其不能葬者十餘喪，天性如此。

translations.literal: Shouchang was bold in righteousness. In relieving others' urgencies he spared nothing. He married off two orphaned girls of his brothers, and buried more than ten coffins of those who could not afford burial—such was his innate character.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang was bold in righteousness and held back nothing when others were in urgent need. He provided dowries for two orphaned nieces, buried more than ten families who could not afford funerals—and such was his nature.

sentences.zh: 侯可，字無可，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Hou Ke, courtesy name Wuke, was a man of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ke, courtesy name Wuke, was a native of Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻不羈，以氣節自許。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and unrestrained, holding himself to a standard of heroic integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was free-spirited and unrestrained, holding himself to a standard of heroic integrity.

sentences.zh: 既壯，盡易前好，篤誌為學。

translations.literal: Once grown, he wholly changed his former pursuits and devoted himself resolutely to study.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he wholly abandoned his former ways and devoted himself resolutely to learning.

sentences.zh: 隨計入京，里中醵金贐行。

translations.literal: He went to the capital for the provincial examination. The village pooled money to assist his journey.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to the capital for the provincial examination, and his neighbors pooled money to assist his journey.

sentences.zh: 比還，悉散其餘與同舉者，曰：「 此金，鄉里所以資應詔者也，不可以為他利。」

translations.literal: When he returned, he distributed the remainder entirely to fellow examinees, saying: "This money is what the village provided to support response to the imperial summons. It may not be used for other profit."
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he distributed the remainder entirely to fellow examinees, saying, "This money is what our neighbors provided to support us in answering the imperial summons. It must not be used for personal gain."

sentences.zh: 且行，聞鄉人病，念曰：「吾歸，則彼死矣！」

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he heard a fellow villager was ill and thought: "If I return home, he will die!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, he heard a fellow villager was ill and thought, "If I go home now, he will die!"

sentences.zh: 遂留不去。

translations.literal: He therefore stayed and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: So he stayed and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 病者愈，輟己馬載之，徒步而歸。

translations.literal: When the sick man recovered, Ke gave up his own horse to carry him and walked home on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When the sick man recovered, Ke gave up his own horse to carry him home and walked back on foot.

sentences.zh: 孫沔征儂徭，請參軍事，奏功得官，知巴州化城縣。

translations.literal: When Sun Mian campaigned against the Nong Yao, Ke requested to participate in military affairs; his reported achievements gained him an office, and he was appointed magistrate of Huacheng County in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Mian campaigned against the Nong Yao, Ke volunteered for his staff; merit he earned in the campaign won him an office, and he was made magistrate of Huacheng County in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 巴俗尚鬼而廢醫，唯巫言是用。

translations.literal: Ba custom revered ghosts and abandoned medicine; only the words of shamans were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In Ba, custom favored spirits over physicians, and only a shaman's word was obeyed.

sentences.zh: 娶婦必責財，貧人女至老不得嫁。

translations.literal: Taking a bride required demanding wealth; daughters of the poor might grow old unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage demanded a bride-price so steep that poor men's daughters often remained unmarried into old age.

sentences.zh: 可為約束，立制度，違者有罪，幾變其習。

translations.literal: Ke established regulations and set up a system; violators were punished, and the customs were nearly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Ke imposed rules and established a system with penalties for violators, and the old ways were nearly transformed.

sentences.zh: 再調華原主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to serve as chief clerk of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to serve as chief clerk of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 富人有不占田籍而質人田券至萬畝，歲責其租。

translations.literal: A wealthy man, though not listed on the land register, held pledged land deeds totaling ten thousand mu and collected annual rent on them.
translations.idiomatic: A rich man who owned no land on the register held others' pledged land deeds totaling ten thousand mu and collected rent on them every year.

sentences.zh: 可晨馳至富家，發櫝出券歸其主。

translations.literal: Ke rode at dawn to the rich man's house, opened the chest, produced the deeds, and returned them to their rightful owners.
translations.idiomatic: Ke rode out at dawn to the rich man's house, opened his chest, took out the deeds, and restored them to their rightful owners.

sentences.zh: 郡吏趙至誠貪狡凶橫，持守以下短長，前後莫能去。

translations.literal: The county clerk Zhao Zhicheng was greedy, cunning, fierce, and overbearing; he held damaging knowledge over the prefect and officials beneath him, and none before or after could remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The county clerk Zhao Zhicheng was greedy, cunning, fierce, and overbearing; he held compromising leverage over the prefect and his subordinates, and no one before or after could get rid of him.

sentences.zh: 可暴其罪，荷校置獄，言於大府誅之，聞者快服。

translations.literal: Ke exposed his crimes, put him in the cangue and prison, reported to the superior prefecture to have him executed; those who heard of it were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ke exposed his crimes, placed him in the cangue and in prison, and petitioned the superior prefecture to have him executed; all who heard of it were gratified and submitted.

sentences.zh: 簽書儀州判官。

translations.literal: He was appointed signing secretary and vice-prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed signing secretary and vice-prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 西夏寇邊，使者使可按視，即以數十騎涉夏境，猝與之遇，亟分其騎為三四，令之曰：「建爾旗幟，旋山徐行。」

translations.literal: When Western Xia raided the border, an envoy was sent for Ke to inspect; he took several dozen horsemen and crossed into Xia territory, suddenly encountering them; he quickly divided his riders into three or four groups and ordered them: "Raise your banners and flags, circle the hills, and proceed slowly."
translations.idiomatic: When Western Xia raided the frontier, an envoy was dispatched for Ke to inspect the situation; he took several dozen horsemen and crossed into Xia territory, where he suddenly encountered the enemy; he quickly split his riders into three or four groups and commanded them, "Raise your banners and flags, circle the hills, and advance slowly."

sentences.zh: 夏人循環間見，疑以為誘騎不敢擊。

translations.literal: The Xia people saw them intermittently as they circled; suspecting they were bait cavalry, they did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: As the Xia troops caught glimpses of them circling round and round, they suspected a decoy force and did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 韓琦鎮長安，薦知涇陽縣。

translations.literal: Han Qi governed Chang'an and recommended Ke to serve as magistrate of Jingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, stationed at Chang'an, recommended Ke for appointment as magistrate of Jingyang County.

sentences.zh: 說渭源羌酋輸地八千頃，因城熟羊以撫之。

translations.literal: He persuaded the Qiang chieftain of Weiyuan to cede eight thousand qing of land, and built the fortified settlement of Shuyang to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the Qiang chieftain of Weiyuan to surrender eight thousand qing of land and built the fortified settlement of Shuyang to win them over.

sentences.zh: 琦上其功。

translations.literal: Qi reported his achievements to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qi memorialized the court with an account of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 又議復鄭白渠，得召對，旋以微罪罷。

translations.literal: He also proposed restoring the Zheng-Bai Canal, was summoned for audience, but soon was dismissed on a minor offense.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed restoring the Zheng-Bai Canal, was summoned for an imperial audience, but was soon dismissed on a minor charge.

sentences.zh: 官至殿中丞，卒於家，年七十二。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Vice Director within the Palace Secretariat and died at home at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director within the Palace Secretariat and died at home at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 可輕財樂義，急人之急，憂人之憂。

translations.literal: Ke lightly regarded wealth and delighted in righteousness; he rushed to others' emergencies and shared others' sorrows.
translations.idiomatic: Ke held wealth lightly and took joy in righteousness; he rushed to others in their emergencies and grieved for others in their troubles.

sentences.zh: 與田顏為友。

translations.literal: He was friends with Tian Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was friends with Tian Yan.

sentences.zh: 顏病重，千里求醫，未歸而顏死，目不瞑。

translations.literal: When Yan fell gravely ill, Ke traveled a thousand li to seek a physician; before he returned Yan died, and his eyes would not close.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell gravely ill, Ke traveled a thousand li to find a physician; before he returned, Yan had died, and his eyes would not close.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「其待侯君乎？」

translations.literal: People said: "Is he waiting for Lord Hou?"
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Is he waiting for Master Hou?"

sentences.zh: 且斂而可至，拊之乃瞑。

translations.literal: When the body was about to be laid in the coffin and Ke arrived, they patted the corpse and only then did the eyes close.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was about to be placed in the coffin and Ke arrived, they patted the corpse and only then did the eyes close.

sentences.zh: 顏無子，不克葬，可辛勤百營，鬻衣相役，卒葬之。

translations.literal: Yan had no son and could not be buried; Ke toiled in every way, sold clothes and worked together with others, and finally succeeded in burying him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had no son and could not be buried; Ke labored tirelessly by every means, selling clothes and working alongside others, until at last the burial was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 方天寒，單衣以居，有饋白金者，顧顏之妹處室，舉以佐其奩具。

translations.literal: It was the depth of winter and he lived in a single layer of clothes; when someone presented white gold, thinking of Yan's unmarried sister, he gave it all to help with her marriage dowry.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter he lived in a single layer of clothing; when someone gave him white gold, he thought of Yan's unmarried sister and gave it all to help furnish her dowry.

sentences.zh: 一日自遠歸，家以窶告，適友人郭行扣門曰：「吾父病，醫邀錢百千，賣吾廬而不售。」

translations.literal: One day returning from afar, his family told him of their poverty; just then his friend Guo Xing knocked at the door and said: "My father is ill; the physician demands a hundred thousand cash; I have tried to sell my hut but cannot."
translations.idiomatic: One day, returning from afar, his family told him how impoverished they were; just then his friend Guo Xing knocked at the door and said, "My father is ill; the physician wants a hundred thousand cash, and I have tried to sell my hut but cannot find a buyer."

sentences.zh: 可惻然，計橐中裝略當其數，盡與之。

translations.literal: Ke was moved with compassion; calculating that what was in his purse roughly matched the sum, he gave it all.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was deeply moved; reckoning that what he had in his purse came to about that sum, he gave it all away.

sentences.zh: 關中稱其賢。

translations.literal: Guanzhong praised him as a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: All of Guanzhong praised him as a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 申積中，成都人。

translations.literal: Shen Jizhong was a man of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jizhong was a native of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 繈褓中，楊繪從其父起求之為子。

translations.literal: While still in swaddling clothes, Yang Hui followed his father to request him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: While still in swaddling clothes, Yang Hui accompanied his father to request him as an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 及長，知非楊氏而絕口不言。

translations.literal: When grown, knowing he was not of the Yang clan, he never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up and learned he was not of the Yang clan, he never spoke a word of it.

sentences.zh: 年十九，登進士第。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 事所養父母，盡孝終身。

translations.literal: He served his adoptive parents with full filial devotion throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: He served his adoptive parents with complete filial devotion for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 有二弟一妹，為畢婚娶，始歸本族，復為申氏，蜀人以純孝歸之。

translations.literal: He had two younger brothers and one sister; after arranging their marriages, he returned to his original clan and resumed the surname Shen; the people of Shu attributed pure filial devotion to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had two younger brothers and one sister; after seeing them all married, he returned to his original clan and resumed the surname Shen, and the people of Shu credited him with pure filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，以奉議郎通判德順軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, he served as acting prefect of Deshun Army with the rank of Fengyi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhenghe era, he served as acting prefect of Deshun Army with the rank of Gentleman for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士許光凝嘗守成都，得其事薦諸朝，召赴京師，擢提舉永興軍學事，道卒。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Xu Guangning had once governed Chengdu and, learning of his story, recommended him to the court; summoned to the capital, he was promoted to superintendent of educational affairs for Yongxing Army, but died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Xu Guangning had once governed Chengdu; learning of his story, he recommended him to the court. Summoned to the capital, he was promoted to superintendent of educational affairs for Yongxing Army, but died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 光凝復與宣和殿學士薛嗣昌、中書舍人宇文黃中表其操行，詔予一子官。

translations.literal: Guangning together with Xuanhe Hall Academician Xue Sichang and Secretariat Drafter Yuwen Huangzhong memorialized his conduct; an edict granted an office to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning, together with Xuanhe Hall Academician Xue Sichang and Secretariat Drafter Yuwen Huangzhong, submitted a memorial praising his conduct, and an edict granted an official post to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 初，光凝所同薦者三人：其一河陽故大理丞陳芳，一門十四世，同居三百年；

translations.literal: At first, of the three men Guangning jointly recommended, one was the former Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Fang of Heyang, whose clan had lived together for fourteen generations across three hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, of the three men Guangning had jointly recommended, one was the former Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Fang of Heyang, whose clan had lived together for fourteen generations over three hundred years;

sentences.zh: 一鄧州王襄，經術登科，年未六十，請老，事孀嫂如母，養孤甥如子，教誨後進，周恤鄉里貧民，以學行稱。

translations.literal: One was Wang Xiang of Dengzhou, who passed the examination through classical learning; before sixty he requested retirement; he served his widowed sister-in-law as a mother, raised his orphaned nephew as a son, instructed younger scholars, and generously aided the poor of his neighborhood, and was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Wang Xiang of Dengzhou, who had passed the examinations through classical learning; before the age of sixty he requested retirement. He served his widowed sister-in-law as a mother, raised his orphaned nephew as a son, instructed younger scholars, and generously aided the poor of his neighborhood, and was renowned for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 乞加獎異。

translations.literal: They requested special awards and distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: They requested that special honors be conferred.

sentences.zh: 詔表芳門閭，賜襄號「處士」。

translations.literal: An edict honored Chen Fang's gateway with an inscribed tablet and bestowed on Wang Xiang the title "Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: An edict honored Chen Fang's gateway with an inscribed tablet and bestowed on Wang Xiang the title Recluse.

sentences.zh: 郝戭，字伯牙，石州定胡人。

translations.literal: Hao Yan, courtesy name Boya, was a man of Dinghu in Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yan, courtesy name Boya, was a native of Dinghu in Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧，竭力營養。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he exerted all his strength to support and nourish them.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he exerted every effort to support and provide for them.

sentences.zh: 或憐傷之，貸以錢數百萬，使取息自贍，戭重謝，留錢五六年不用，復返之。

translations.literal: Someone pitying him lent him several million cash for him to live on the interest; Yan deeply declined, kept the money five or six years unused, then returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who pitied him lent him several million cash so he could live on the interest; Yan earnestly declined, kept the money five or six years without using it, and then returned it.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調宛丘尉、舞陽主簿、通山令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Wanshill assistant commandant, Wuyang chief clerk, and Tongshan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant commandant of Wanshill, chief clerk of Wuyang, and magistrate of Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 時年未五十，以父樵老不第，上書請致仕，為父求官。

translations.literal: Though not yet fifty, because his father Qiao was old and had never passed the examinations, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement to seek an office for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Though not yet fifty, because his father Qiao was old and had never passed the examinations, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement so that he might obtain an office for his father.

sentences.zh: 執政諭使赴官而後請，曰：「如是，則可升朝籍，遇恩及親矣。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers instructed him to take office first and then make the request, saying: "In that way you can enter the court register and when favors come, your parents will receive them too."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers advised him to take office first and then make his request, saying, "In that way you can enter the court register, and when imperial favors are granted, your parents will share in them as well."

sentences.zh: 於是留妻子於家，獨奉父行，逾歲竟謝事。

translations.literal: He therefore left his wife and children at home, traveled alone with his father, and after more than a year finally resigned from office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore left his wife and children at home, traveled alone with his father, and after more than a year finally resigned from office.

sentences.zh: 上官以其治縣有績，惜其去，固留之；

translations.literal: His superiors, seeing his accomplishments in administering the county, regretted his departure and firmly tried to detain him;
translations.idiomatic: His superiors, impressed by his achievements in governing the county, regretted his departure and tried hard to keep him;

sentences.zh: 耆老拜庭遮道，皆不能止。

translations.literal: Elders bowed in the courtyard and blocked the road, yet none could stop him.
translations.idiomatic: The elders bowed in the courtyard and blocked the road, but none could stop him.

sentences.zh: 得太子中允以歸，未至鄉里而樵卒。

translations.literal: He obtained the post of Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household and returned home, but before reaching his hometown Qiao died.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained the post of Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household and set out for home, but before he reached his hometown his father Qiao died.

sentences.zh: 自畚土造塚，人有助之者，使置土塚上，去則隨撤之。

translations.literal: He built the tomb himself with a basket and shovel; when others offered help, he had them place earth on the mound, and when they left he immediately removed it.
translations.idiomatic: He built the tomb himself with basket and shovel; when others offered help, he had them place earth on the mound, and as soon as they left he removed it.

sentences.zh: 服除，州以狀聞，詔賜粟帛。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the prefecture reported the circumstances; an edict bestowed grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, the prefecture reported his circumstances to the court, and an edict bestowed grain and silk upon him.

sentences.zh: 治平末，以翰林學士呂公著薦，起為奉寧軍推官，涇原經略使亦奏辟幕府。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiping era, on recommendation of Hanlin Academician Lü Gongzhu, he was summoned as judicial officer of Fengning Army; the Jingyuan frontier commissioner also memorialized to recruit him to the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiping era, on the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Lü Gongzhu, he was summoned to serve as judicial officer of Fengning Army, and the Jingyuan frontier commissioner also memorialized to recruit him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 戭曰：「向所以未老致仕，欲官及親也。

translations.literal: Yan said: "The reason I retired before old age was that I wished an office might reach my parents.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "The reason I retired before I was old was that I wanted an office to reach my parents while they lived.

sentences.zh: 既不能及，尚庶幾以恩得贈，今則無及矣！」

translations.literal: Since that could not be achieved, I still hoped perhaps through imperial grace to receive posthumous honors for them—but now there is no chance!"
translations.idiomatic: Since that could not be achieved, I still hoped that through imperial grace they might receive posthumous honors—but now even that is beyond reach!"

sentences.zh: 姻族語其妻聶氏，使勸戭仕，曰：「吾不德，無以助君子，矧敢強其所不欲以累其高哉。」

translations.literal: Relatives told his wife Lady Nie to urge Yan to take office; she said: "I lack virtue and cannot assist my lord—how much less dare I force what he does not wish and burden his lofty integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: Relatives spoke to his wife Lady Nie and urged her to persuade Yan to take office; she said, "I lack virtue and have no way to assist my husband—how much less would I dare force upon him what he does not wish and burden his lofty integrity!"

sentences.zh: 聶事舅姑亦以孝義著。

translations.literal: Nie also served her parents-in-law with renowned filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Nie also served her parents-in-law with renowned filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 戭忠信自將，篤行苦節，不仕而卒。

translations.literal: Yan maintained himself with loyalty and trustworthiness, practiced steadfast conduct and bitter integrity, held no office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan conducted himself with loyalty and trustworthiness, practiced steadfast conduct and austere integrity, held no office, and died.

sentences.zh: 司馬光為銘其墓。

translations.literal: Simu Guang wrote the epitaph for his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Simu Guang composed the epitaph for his tomb.

sentences.zh: 支漸，資州資陽人。

translations.literal: Zhi Jian was a man of Ziyang in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Jian was a native of Ziyang in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 年七十，持母喪，既葬，廬墓側，負土成墳，蓬首垢麵，三時號泣，哀毀瘠甚。

translations.literal: At seventy he observed mourning for his mother; after the burial he built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to form the mound, wore disheveled hair and a grimy face, wailed through the three mourning seasons, and grieved until he was emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he observed mourning for his mother; after the burial he built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to raise the mound, wore disheveled hair and a grimy face, wailed through the three mourning seasons, and grieved himself into emaciation.

sentences.zh: 白蛇狸兔擾其旁，白雀白烏日集於壟木，五色雀至萬餘，回翔悲鳴若助哀者。

translations.literal: White snakes and foxes lingered nearby; white magpies and white crows daily gathered on the tomb trees; more than ten thousand multicolored finches came, wheeling and crying mournfully as if aiding his grief.
translations.idiomatic: White snakes and foxes hovered nearby; white magpies and white crows gathered daily on the trees above the mound; more than ten thousand multicolored finches arrived, wheeling and crying mournfully as though sharing his grief.

sentences.zh: 鄉人句文鼎自娶婦即與父母離居，睹漸至行，深自悔責，號慟而歸，孝養盡誌。

translations.literal: Fellow villager Ju Wenting had lived apart from his parents since taking a wife; witnessing Jian's conduct, he deeply blamed himself, wailing returned home, and devoted himself wholly to filial care.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow villager, Ju Wenting, had lived apart from his parents ever since taking a wife; witnessing Jian's conduct, he deeply reproached himself, wailing returned home, and devoted himself wholly to filial care.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭觀感而化者甚眾。

translations.literal: Very many in the village were moved by the sight and transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Very many in the village were moved by what they saw and changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 鄧宗古，簡州陽安人。

translations.literal: Deng Zonggu was a man of Yang'an in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zonggu was a native of Yang'an in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 父死，自培土為墳，廬其側，晨夕號慟，甘露降於墓木。

translations.literal: When his father died, he mounded earth himself for the tomb, built a hut beside it, wailed morning and evening, and sweet dew descended on the tomb trees.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he mounded the earth for the tomb himself, built a hut beside it, and wailed morning and evening; sweet dew descended on the trees above the grave.

sentences.zh: 里中號為鄧孝子。

translations.literal: The village called him Filial Son Deng.
translations.idiomatic: The village called him Filial Son Deng.

sentences.zh: 沈宣，汝州梁人。

translations.literal: Shen Xuan was a man of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xuan was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 母亡，既葬，不塞墓門三十有六月，晝負土，夜拊棺而臥，為墳廣百尺。

translations.literal: When his mother died, after burial he did not seal the tomb entrance for thirty-six months; by day he carried earth, by night he slept beside the coffin stroking it, and made the mound a hundred chi broad.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, after the burial he did not seal the tomb entrance for thirty-six months; by day he carried earth, by night he slept beside the coffin stroking it, and he made the mound a hundred chi broad.

sentences.zh: 妻高氏亦有孝行。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Gao also practiced filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Gao, also practiced filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 漸以下三人，元豐中，皆褒賜粟帛。

translations.literal: The three men below Jian—in the Yuanfeng era, all were praised and awarded grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The three men below Jian—in the Yuanfeng era, all were commended and granted grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 蘇慶文、台亨，皆夏縣人。

translations.literal: Su Qingwen and Tai Heng were both men of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qingwen and Tai Heng were both natives of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 慶文事父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Qingwen was known for serving his parents with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Qingwen was renowned for serving his parents with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 母少寡，慶文懼其妻不能敬事，每戒之曰：「汝事吾母，少不謹必逐汝。」

translations.literal: His mother had been widowed young; Qingwen feared his wife might not serve her respectfully and regularly warned her: "In serving my mother, if you are the least remiss I shall drive you out."
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been widowed young; Qingwen feared his wife might not serve her respectfully and regularly warned her, "In serving my mother, if you are the least bit remiss I shall drive you out."

sentences.zh: 妻奉教，母得安其室終身。

translations.literal: The wife followed his instruction, and the mother lived peacefully in the household to the end of her days.
translations.idiomatic: The wife obeyed his instruction, and the mother lived peacefully in the household for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 亨工畫，元豐中，朝廷修景靈宮，調天下畫工詣京師，選試其優者待詔翰林，畀以官祿，亨名第一。

translations.literal: Heng was skilled in painting; in the Yuanfeng era the court restored the Jingling Palace and summoned painters from across the realm to the capital; the best were selected as Hanlin attendants and granted office and salary; Heng ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was skilled in painting; in the Yuanfeng era, when the court restored the Jingling Palace, painters from across the realm were summoned to the capital, and the best were selected as Hanlin attendants and granted office and salary; Heng ranked first.

sentences.zh: 以父老固辭歸養，閭里賢之。

translations.literal: Because his father was old he firmly declined and returned to support him; neighbors praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was old, he firmly declined the appointment and returned home to support him; neighbors praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 仰忻，字天貺，溫州永嘉人。

translations.literal: Yang Xin, courtesy name Tiankuang, was a man of Yongjia in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin, courtesy name Tiankuang, was a native of Yongjia in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 力學，以篤行稱。

translations.literal: He studied diligently and was known for steadfast conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He studied diligently and was known for steadfast conduct.

sentences.zh: 年五十餘，執母喪盡孝禮。

translations.literal: Past fifty, he observed his mother's mourning with complete filial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Past the age of fifty, he observed his mother's mourning with complete filial rites.

sentences.zh: 躬自負土，廬於墓側，有慈烏白竹之瑞。

translations.literal: He personally carried earth, built a hut beside the tomb, and there were auspicious signs of compassionate crows and white bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He personally carried earth and built a hut beside the tomb; there were auspicious signs of compassionate crows and white bamboo.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，郡守楊蟠表其裏「孝廉坊」。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era, prefect Yang Pan had his neighborhood honored with the plaque "Filial and Incorruptible."
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era, Prefect Yang Pan had his neighborhood honored with the plaque Filial and Incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，以行取士，郡以忻應詔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, when men were selected by conduct, the prefecture nominated Xin in response to the decree.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Daguan era, when officials were selected on the basis of conduct, the prefecture nominated Xin in response to the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，特贈將仕郎。

translations.literal: Before long he died; he was specially granted the posthumous rank of Junior Gentleman for Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; he was specially granted the posthumous rank of Junior Gentleman for Merit.

sentences.zh: 趙伯深，字逢原。

translations.literal: Zhao Boshen, courtesy name Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Boshen, courtesy name Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 父子佪，宣和間為棣州兵官屬。

translations.literal: His father Zibian, during the Xuanhe era, served as a military staff officer in Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zibian, during the Xuanhe era, served on the military staff in Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 會兵動燕雲，子佪被檄往塞上。

translations.literal: When troops moved on Yan-Yun, Zibian was ordered by dispatch to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were mobilized for Yan-Yun, Zibian was dispatched by order to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 伯深時尚幼，與其母張留居棣州。

translations.literal: Boshen was still young and remained in Dizhou with his mother Lady Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Boshen was still young and remained in Dizhou with his mother, Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 既而金人渡河，伯深母子相失。

translations.literal: Soon the Jurchens crossed the river; Boshen and his mother became separated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jurchens crossed the river, and Boshen and his mother were separated.

sentences.zh: 子佪亦隔絕，建炎二年，始得南歸。

translations.literal: Zibian was also cut off; in the second year of Jianyan he finally returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Zibian was also cut off from them; in the second year of the Jianyan era he finally returned south.

sentences.zh: 子佪卒，伯深訪尋其母二十餘年。

translations.literal: Zibian died; Boshen searched for his mother for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Zibian died, and Boshen searched for his mother for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 一旦聞在滬南，伯深徒步入蜀，間關累年。

translations.literal: One day learning she was south of the Hu, Boshen walked on foot into Shu, enduring hardships for many years.
translations.idiomatic: One day he learned she was south of the Hu River; Boshen walked on foot into Shu, enduring hardships for many years.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年，乃得其母，相持號泣，哀感行路。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Shaoxing he finally found his mother; they clung to each other wailing, moving all who passed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Shaoxing era he finally found his mother; they clung to each other wailing, moving all who passed on the road to tears.

sentences.zh: 曾慥在夔州，賦詩以美其孝。

translations.literal: Zeng Zao, while in Kuizhou, composed a poem praising his filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Zao, while serving in Kuizhou, composed a poem praising his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 彭瑜，字君玉，吉之安福人。

translations.literal: Peng Yu, courtesy name Junyu, was a man of Anfu in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yu, courtesy name Junyu, was a native of Anfu in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 熙寧間失其母，瑜朝夕焚香祈天，願知母所在，如是十餘年。

translations.literal: During the Xining era he lost track of his mother; Yu burned incense day and night praying to Heaven to learn where she was—thus for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he lost track of his mother; Yu burned incense morning and evening, praying to Heaven to learn where she was, and did so for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 俄有人言母為泰和倪氏婦，瑜竟迎以歸。

translations.literal: Suddenly someone said his mother had become the wife of the Ni clan of Taihe; Yu went and brought her home.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly someone said his mother had become a wife of the Ni clan in Taihe; Yu went at once and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 毛洵字子仁，吉州吉水人。

translations.literal: Mao Xun, courtesy name Ziren, was a man of Jishui in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xun, courtesy name Ziren, was a native of Jishui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年進士，又中拔萃科。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng he passed the jinshi examination and also passed the special selection examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tiansheng era he passed the jinshi examination and also passed the special selection examination.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，凡守四官，再以親疾解任，執藥調膳，嘗而後進，三月不之寢室。

translations.literal: His nature was profoundly filial; of the four offices he held, twice he resigned on account of a parent's illness; he prepared medicine and meals, tasted them before serving, and for three months did not enter the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was profoundly filial; of the four offices he held, twice he resigned on account of a parent's illness. He prepared medicine and meals, tasted them before serving them, and for three months at a time did not enter the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 父應佺通判太平州，卒官，母高繼卒於池陽舟次。

translations.literal: His father Yingquan served as vice prefect of Taiping Prefecture and died in office; his mother Gao Ji died at Chiyang while their boat was moored.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingquan had served as vice prefect of Taiping Prefecture and died in office; his mother Gao Ji died at Chiyang while their boat was still at anchor.

sentences.zh: 持鍤荷土以為墳，手胝麵黔，親友不能識，廬於墓凡二十一月，朝夕哭踴，食裁脫粟。

translations.literal: He took up a spade and carried earth to make tombs; his hands grew calloused and his face darkened until kin and friends could not recognize him. He lived in a hut at the graves for twenty-one months in all, weeping and stamping in grief morning and evening, eating only husked millet.
translations.idiomatic: He took up a spade and carried earth to build the tombs himself. His hands grew calloused and his face turned dark until relatives and friends could no longer recognize him. He lived in a hut beside the graves for twenty-one months in all, weeping and stamping in grief morning and evening, and ate nothing but husked millet.

sentences.zh: 諸生請問經義，對之流涕，未嘗言文。

translations.literal: When students asked about the meaning of the classics, he answered them in tears and never spoke of literary matters.
translations.idiomatic: When fellow students asked him about the meaning of the classics, he would answer in tears and never speak of literary pursuits.

sentences.zh: 抱疾歸，數日而卒。

translations.literal: He returned home ill and died after several days.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home ill and died within a few days.

sentences.zh: 郡以孝聞，賜其家帛五十匹、米五十斛。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported his filial piety; his household was granted fifty bolts of silk and fifty hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported his filial devotion to the court, and his family was granted fifty bolts of silk and fifty hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 兄溥，字文祖，亦以哀毀卒於舟中。

translations.literal: His elder brother Pu, courtesy name Wenzu, also died on a boat from excessive grief.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Pu, courtesy name Wenzu, likewise died aboard a boat from grief that had wasted his body.

sentences.zh: 李籌者，洵同縣人，字彥良。

translations.literal: Li Chou was a man of the same county as Xun, courtesy name Yanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chou was a native of the same county as Mao Xun, courtesy name Yanliang.

sentences.zh: 與弟衡字平國生同乳，二歲喪母，十歲喪父，兄弟每以不逮事親為恨。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Heng, courtesy name Pingguo, were nursed by the same woman. They lost their mother at two and their father at ten; the brothers always regretted that they had not been able to serve their parents.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Heng, courtesy name Pingguo, had shared the same wet nurse. They lost their mother at the age of two and their father at ten, and the brothers always grieved that they had never had the chance to serve their parents properly.

sentences.zh: 政和中，改葬其母於楊山，負土成墳，廬於墓左。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era he reburied his mother on Yang Mountain, carried earth to form the tomb, and built a hut to the left of the grave.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era he reburied his mother on Yang Mountain, carried earth to build the tomb himself, and lived in a hut to the left of the grave.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廬所產木一本兩幹，高丈許復合於一，至其末乃分兩幹五枝，鄉人以為瑞。

translations.literal: Before long a tree grew at the hut site with one root and two trunks; about a zhang high they merged into one, and at the top split again into two trunks with five branches. The villagers took it as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a tree sprang up at the hut with one root and two trunks. About a zhang in height the trunks merged into one, then at the top divided again into two trunks bearing five branches. The villagers regarded it as an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 有楊芾者，亦同縣人，字文卿，性至孝，歸必市酒肉以奉二親，未嘗及妻子。

translations.literal: There was Yang Fei, also of the same county, courtesy name Wenqing, whose nature was profoundly filial. Whenever he returned home he would buy wine and meat to serve both parents and never let his wife and children have any first.
translations.idiomatic: There was Yang Fei, also of the same county, courtesy name Wenqing, whose nature was profoundly filial. Whenever he came home he would buy wine and meat for both parents and never spared any for his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年大饑，為親負米百里外，遇盜奪之不與，盜欲兵之，芾慟哭曰：「吾為親負米，不食三日矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, during a great famine, he carried rice for his parents from a hundred li away. He met a bandit who tried to seize it and he would not yield; the bandit was about to strike him with a weapon. Fei wailed and said, "I am carrying rice for my parents and have not eaten for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Shaoxing era, during a great famine, he carried rice for his parents from a hundred li away. He met a bandit who tried to rob him of it and he refused to give it up; the bandit was about to attack him with a weapon. Fei wept aloud and said, "I am carrying this rice for my parents and have not eaten for three days.

sentences.zh: 幸哀我。」

translations.literal: Please pity me."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to take pity on me."

sentences.zh: 盜義而釋之。

translations.literal: The bandit was moved by his righteousness and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit was moved by his righteousness and let him go.

sentences.zh: 楊慶，鄞人。

translations.literal: Yang Qing was a man of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 父病，貧不能召醫，乃刲股肉啖之，良已。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, the family was too poor to summon a physician, so he cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to him; his father soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, the family was too poor to call a physician, so he cut flesh from his own thigh and fed it to him; his father soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 其後母病不能食，慶取右乳焚之，以灰和藥進焉，入口遂差，久之乳復生。
