translations.literal: Later his mother fell ill and could not eat. Qing took his right breast, burned it, mixed the ash with medicine, and gave it to her; as soon as she swallowed it she recovered, and after a long while the breast grew back.
translations.idiomatic: Later his mother fell ill and could not eat. Qing cut off his right breast, burned it, mixed the ash with medicine, and gave it to her; as soon as she took it she recovered, and in time the breast grew back.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，守樓異名其坊曰「崇孝」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe, the prefect Lou Yi named his ward "Revering Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xuanhe era, Prefect Lou Yi named his neighborhood the Revering Filial Piety Ward.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，守仇悆為之請。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing, the prefect Qiu Yu petitioned on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Shaoxing era, Prefect Qiu Yu submitted a memorial on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔表其門，復之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year an edict honored his gate and granted him exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year an imperial edict ordered his gate honored and granted his household tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 悆曰：「韓退之作《鄠人對》，以毀傷支體為害義。

translations.literal: Qiu said, "Han Tuizhi wrote 'The Response from the Man of E,' holding that mutilating the body harms righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yu said, "Han Yu wrote The Response from the Man of E, arguing that mutilating one's body violates righteousness.

sentences.zh: 而匹夫單人，身膏草莽，軌訓之理未宏，汲引之徒多闕，而乃行成於內，情發自天。

translations.literal: Yet for a lone common man whose body lies buried in the wild grass, the norms of instruction are not widely spread and those who guide and uplift are many times lacking—yet conduct is perfected within and feeling arises from Heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a solitary commoner whose body may lie buried in the wild grass, the norms of moral instruction are not widely taught and those who guide and uplift others are often absent—yet his conduct was perfected within and his feeling sprang from Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 使稍知詩書禮義之說，推其所存，出身事主，臨難伏節死義，豈減介之推、安金藏哉！」

translations.literal: Had he known even a little of the teachings of the classics, ritual, and righteousness, and extended what he possessed—going forth to serve his lord, facing hardship upholding integrity and dying for righteousness—would he not have been the equal of Jie Zhitui and An Jinzang!"
translations.idiomatic: Had he known even a little of the teachings of the classics, ritual, and righteousness, and carried what he possessed to its full extent—going forth to serve his sovereign, facing hardship with steadfast integrity and dying for righteousness—would he not have stood equal to Jie Zhitui and An Jinzang!"

sentences.zh: 陳宗，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Chen Zong was a man of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zong was a native of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 年十六，母蔡病篤，刲股為餌，病愈。

translations.literal: At sixteen his mother Lady Cai was gravely ill; he cut flesh from his thigh to make medicine for her, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixteen his mother Lady Cai fell gravely ill; he cut flesh from his thigh to make medicine for her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 已而復病不救，宗一慟而絕。

translations.literal: Soon she relapsed and could not be saved; Zong died in a single burst of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she relapsed and could not be saved; Zong died in one convulsion of grief.

sentences.zh: 郡守陸德輿云：「陳宗自毀其體，哀慟傷生，雖非孝道之正，而能為人所難為之事，亦天性之至。」

translations.literal: The prefect Lu Deyu said, "Chen Zong destroyed his own body and grief harmed his life; though this is not the proper way of filial piety, yet in doing what others find hard to do he reached the utmost of natural disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Lu Deyu said, "Chen Zong mutilated his own body and grief destroyed his life; though this is not the orthodox path of filial piety, in doing what others find impossible he reached the utmost of natural feeling.

sentences.zh: 官為合葬，榜曰「陳孝子墓」。

translations.literal: The authorities gave them a joint burial and posted a plaque reading "Tomb of the Filial Son Chen."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities gave them a joint burial and erected a plaque reading Tomb of the Filial Son Chen."

sentences.zh: 郭義，興化軍人。

translations.literal: Guo Yi was a man of Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was a native of Xinghua Army.

sentences.zh: 早遊太學，以操尚稱。

translations.literal: He studied early at the Imperial Academy and was renowned for his integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy at a young age and was known for the integrity of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，客錢塘，聞母喪，徒跣奔喪，每一慟輒嘔血。

translations.literal: Past forty he was staying in Qiantang; when he heard of his mother's death he ran barefoot to mourn, and with each burst of grief he vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: Past the age of forty he was staying in Qiantang; when he heard of his mother's death he ran home barefoot to mourn, and each time grief seized him he vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 家貧甚，故人有所饋，不受。

translations.literal: His family was extremely poor; when old friends offered gifts he would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: His family was extremely poor, and when old friends offered gifts he refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 聚土為墳，手蒔鬆竹，而廬於其旁。

translations.literal: He piled earth to make the tomb, personally planted pine and bamboo, and built a hut beside it.
translations.idiomatic: He piled earth to build the tomb, planted pine and bamboo with his own hands, and lived in a hut beside it.

sentences.zh: 甘露降於墓上，烏鵲馴集。

translations.literal: Sweet dew fell upon the tomb, and crows and magpies gathered there tame.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew fell upon the tomb, and crows and magpies gathered there tamely.

sentences.zh: 郡上其事，詔旌表其閭，於所居前安綽楔，左右建土台，高一丈二尺，方正，下廣上狹，飾白，間以赤，仍植所宜木。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported the matter; an edict ordered his neighborhood honored. Before his residence honor posts were installed, and earthen platforms were built on either side, one zhang and two chi high, square, wide below and narrow above, decorated in white interspersed with red, and suitable trees were planted as well.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported the matter to the court, and an imperial edict ordered his neighborhood honored. Honor posts were erected before his residence, and earthen platforms were built on either side, one zhang and two chi in height, square in form, wide at the base and narrow at the top, decorated in white with red accents, and appropriate trees were planted as well.

sentences.zh: 申世寧，信州鉛山人。

translations.literal: Shen Shining was a man of Qianshan in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shining was a native of Qianshan in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，潘達兵襲鉛山，父愈年七十，未及出戶遇賊，賊意其有藏金，欲殺之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, the troops of Pan Da raided Qianshan. His father Yu was seventy and, before he could leave the door, met the bandits. The bandits suspected he had hidden gold and wanted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Shaoxing era, the troops of Pan Da raided Qianshan. His father Yu was seventy years old and, before he could step outside, encountered the bandits. They suspected he had hidden gold and intended to kill him.

sentences.zh: 世寧年未冠，亟引頸願代父死，賊感其孝，兩全之。

translations.literal: Shining was not yet capped in age; he quickly stretched out his neck and offered to die in his father's place. The bandits were moved by his filial piety and spared them both.
translations.idiomatic: Shining was not yet twenty; he quickly bared his neck and offered to die in his father's place. The bandits were moved by his filial devotion and spared them both.

sentences.zh: 苟與齡字壽隆，滁州來安人。

translations.literal: Gou Yuling, courtesy name Shoulong, was a man of Laian in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yuling, courtesy name Shoulong, was a native of Laian in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 誌尚高潔，事其親，生養死葬，力竭而禮盡，鄉黨稱之。

translations.literal: His aspirations were lofty and pure. In serving his parents he sustained them in life and buried them in death, exhausting his strength and fulfilling every rite; the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His aspirations were lofty and pure. In serving his parents he sustained them in life and buried them in death, exhausting his strength and fulfilling every rite, and the whole community praised him.

sentences.zh: 母歿，廬墓側，有芝十九莖生於墓亭。

translations.literal: When his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb; nineteen stalks of lingzhi grew at the tomb pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he lived in a hut beside the tomb, and nineteen stalks of lingzhi mushroom grew at the tomb pavilion.

sentences.zh: 郡縣以事聞，旌其門。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county reported the matter, and his gate was honored.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county reported the matter to the court, and his gate was honored.

sentences.zh: 王珠字仲淵，吉州龍泉人，以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a man of Longquan in Jizhou, known for filial piety and carefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a native of Longquan in Jizhou, renowned for filial piety and careful conduct.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，居父憂，芝數本生墓側，倒植竹以為杙，復生柯葉。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era, while in mourning for his father, several lingzhi grew beside the tomb; he inverted bamboo to serve as stakes, and they sprouted branches and leaves again.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era, while mourning his father, several lingzhi mushrooms grew beside the tomb; he planted bamboo upside down to serve as stakes, and they sprouted branches and leaves anew.

sentences.zh: 紹興間，再罹母喪，復有雙竹靈芝之祥。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era he again suffered his mother's death, and once more there were auspicious signs of twin bamboo and lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era he mourned his mother a second time, and once again there were auspicious signs of twin bamboo and lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 顏詡，唐太師真卿之後。

translations.literal: Yan Xu was a descendant of Yan Zhenqing, Grand Mentor of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xu was a descendant of Yan Zhenqing, Grand Mentor of Tang.

sentences.zh: 真卿嘗謫廬陵，故詡為吉州永新人。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was once exiled to Luling, hence Xu was a man of Yongxin in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing had once been exiled to Luling, and so Xu was a native of Yongxin in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 詡少孤，兄弟數人，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xu was orphaned young; he and his several brothers served their stepmother and were famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xu lost his father while still young; he and his several brothers served their stepmother and were renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 一門千指，家法嚴肅，男女異序，少長輯睦，匜架無主，廚饌不異。

translations.literal: One household counted a thousand fingers; household rules were strict and solemn, men and women kept separate order, young and old lived in harmony, wash basins had no assigned owners, and food from the kitchen was undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: The household numbered a thousand mouths; its rules were strict and solemn, men and women kept to their proper places, young and old lived in harmony, wash basins belonged to no one in particular, and food from the kitchen was shared without distinction.

sentences.zh: 義居數十年，終日怡愉，家人不見其喜慍。

translations.literal: They lived together in righteousness for decades; all day he was cheerful and content, and his family never saw him show anger or delight.
translations.idiomatic: They lived together in communal harmony for decades; all day long he was cheerful and at ease, and his family never saw him show anger or delight.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘卒。

translations.literal: He died past seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 張伯威，大安軍人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bowei was a man of Da'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bowei was a native of Da'an Army.

sentences.zh: 武翼大夫、御前前軍正將祥之子。

translations.literal: He was the son of Xiang, Military Gentleman of Martial Hawk Feathers and Chief Commander of the Front Army of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Xiang, who held the rank of Military Gentleman of Martial Hawk Feathers and served as chief commander of the front army of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，武舉進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he passed the military examination as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shaoxi era he passed the military examination and received the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 調神泉尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Shenquan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Shenquan.

sentences.zh: 大母黃，年九十八，不忍之官。

translations.literal: His grandmother Lady Huang was ninety-eight, and he could not bear to take office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Huang was ninety-eight years old, and he could not bear to leave her and take up his post.

sentences.zh: 黃得血痢疾瀕殆，伯威剔左臂肉食之，遂愈。

translations.literal: Lady Huang contracted bloody dysentery and was near death; Bowei scraped flesh from his left arm for her to eat, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huang contracted bloody dysentery and was near death; Bowei cut flesh from his left arm for her to eat, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 繼母楊因姑病篤，驚而成疾，伯威復剔臂肉作粥以進，其疾亦愈。

translations.literal: His stepmother Lady Yang, because his grandmother's illness was grave, was frightened into falling ill herself; Bowei again scraped flesh from his arm, made porridge, and gave it to her, and her illness also healed.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Lady Yang, alarmed by the gravity of his grandmother's illness, fell ill herself; Bowei again cut flesh from his arm, made porridge, and gave it to her, and she too recovered.

sentences.zh: 伯威妹嫁崔均，其姑王疾，妹亦剔左臂肉作粥以進，達旦即愈。

translations.literal: Bowe's sister had married Cui Jun; when her mother-in-law Lady Wang fell ill, the sister also scraped flesh from her left arm, made porridge, and gave it to her; by dawn she had recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bowe's sister had married Cui Jun; when her mother-in-law Lady Wang fell ill, the sister likewise cut flesh from her left arm, made porridge, and gave it to her, and by dawn she had recovered.

sentences.zh: 知大安軍羅植即伯威所居立純孝坊，崔均所居立孝婦坊。

translations.literal: Luo Zhi, prefect of Da'an Army, established the Pure Filial Piety Ward at Bowei's residence and the Filial Woman Ward at Cui Jun's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhi, military prefect of Da'an Army, established the Pure Filial Piety Ward at Bowei's residence and the Filial Woman Ward at Cui Jun's residence.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔伯威與升擢，倍賜其妹束帛。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered Bowei promoted with elevation and doubled the silk gift to his sister.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the court, an imperial edict ordered Bowei promoted and granted an elevated appointment, and doubled the silk gift to his sister.

sentences.zh: 蔡定，字元應，越州會稽人。

translations.literal: Cai Ding, courtesy name Yuanying, was a man of Kuaiji in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ding, courtesy name Yuanying, was a native of Kuaiji in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家世微且貧。

translations.literal: His family lineage was humble and poor.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble origin and poor.

sentences.zh: 父革，依郡獄吏傭書以生，資定使學，遊鄉校，稍稍有稱。

translations.literal: His father Ge relied on a county prison clerk for copywork to make a living, supported Ding in his studies, and sent him to the district school, where he gradually gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge made a living doing copywork for a county prison clerk, supported Ding in his studies, and sent him to the district school, where he gradually came to be spoken of with respect.

sentences.zh: 郡獄吏一日坐舞文法被係，革以詿誤，年七十餘矣，法當免係。

translations.literal: One day the county prison clerk was charged with twisting the law and imprisoned; Ge was implicated through error. He was over seventy, and by law should have been exempt from imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: One day the county prison clerk was charged with twisting the law and imprisoned; Ge was implicated through a mistake. He was over seventy, and by law should have been exempt from imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 鞫胥任澤削其籍年而入之，罪且與獄吏等。

translations.literal: The interrogating clerk Ren Ze reduced his registered age and entered him as guilty; his punishment was to equal that of the prison clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogating clerk Ren Ze reduced his registered age and entered him as guilty, so that his punishment would equal that of the prison clerk.

sentences.zh: 案具，府奏上之。

translations.literal: When the case was complete the prefecture memorialized it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, the prefecture memorialized it to the court.

sentences.zh: 方待命於朝，故俱久囚，而革不得獨決。

translations.literal: They were awaiting orders from the court, and so both remained long imprisoned, while Ge could not be decided separately.
translations.idiomatic: They were awaiting orders from the court, and so both remained imprisoned for a long time, while Ge could not be released on his own.

sentences.zh: 定切痛念父當耆年，以非辜墮圄狴，誓將身贖。

translations.literal: Ding was deeply pained, thinking that his father in his old age had fallen into prison through no crime, and vowed to redeem him with his own body.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was deeply anguished that his father in old age had fallen into prison through no fault of his own, and vowed to redeem him with his own life.

sentences.zh: 數詣府號訴，請代坐獄，弗許；

translations.literal: Repeatedly he went to the prefecture wailing in petition, asking to substitute for his father in prison; this was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he went to the prefectural office wailing in petition, asking to take his father's place in prison; this was refused;

sentences.zh: 請效命於戎行，弗許；

translations.literal: he asked to offer his life in military service; this was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: he asked to offer his life in military service; this was refused;

sentences.zh: 請隸五符為兵，又弗許。

translations.literal: he asked to be enrolled as a soldier under the Five Talismans; again this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to be enrolled as a soldier under the Five Talismans; again this was refused.

sentences.zh: 定知父終不可贖也，仰而呼曰：「天乎！

translations.literal: Ding knew his father could ultimately not be redeemed; he looked up and cried, "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Ding knew his father could never be redeemed; he looked up to Heaven and cried, "O Heaven!

sentences.zh: 將使定坐視父纏徽纆乎！

translations.literal: Would you have Ding sit and watch his father bound in fetters!
translations.idiomatic: Would you have me sit by and watch my father bound in fetters!

sentences.zh: 父老耄，不應連係；

translations.literal: My father is old and senile and should not be jointly imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: My father is old and frail and should not be imprisoned together with another;

sentences.zh: 傭書，罪不應與獄吏等。

translations.literal: copywork—his crime should not equal that of the prison clerk.
translations.idiomatic: he did copywork—his offense should not be treated as equal to that of the prison clerk.

sentences.zh: 理明矣，而無所雲訴。

translations.literal: The right is clear, yet there is nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The justice of the case is clear, yet there is nowhere I can appeal.

sentences.zh: 父老而刑，定之生其何益乎？

translations.literal: If my father is old and punished, what good is Ding's life?
translations.idiomatic: If my father grows old in punishment, what good is my life to anyone?

sentences.zh: 定圖死矣，庶有司哀憐而釋父，則雖死無憾矣！」

translations.literal: Ding intends to die; perhaps the authorities will pity him and release his father—then though he dies he will have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: I mean to die; perhaps the authorities will take pity and release my father—then even in death I shall have no regret!

sentences.zh: 於是預為誌銘其墓，又為狀若詣府者結置袂間，皆敘陳致死之由，冀其父之必免也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beforehand wrote an epitaph for his tomb and also prepared a petition as if going to the prefecture, folded and placed in his sleeve; all narrated the reasons for his death, hoping his father would surely be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wrote in advance an epitaph for his own grave and also prepared a petition as if he were going to the prefectural office, folded it, and placed it in his sleeve; all of it set forth the reasons for his death, in the hope that his father would surely be released.

sentences.zh: 以建炎元年十二月甲申，自赴河死。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jianyan he drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the twelfth month in the first year of the Jianyan era he drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 府帥聞之，驚曰「真孝」，立命出革，厚為定具棺斂事，而撫周其家。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander heard of it, exclaimed "True filial piety," immediately ordered Ge released, generously prepared coffin and burial for Ding, and comforted and provided for his family.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural commander heard of it, exclaimed, "True filial piety," immediately ordered Ge released, generously arranged coffin and burial for Ding, and comforted and provided for his family.

sentences.zh: 鄭綺，婺州浦江人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi was a man of Pujiang in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi was a native of Pujiang in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善讀書，通《春秋穀梁》學。

translations.literal: He was skilled in reading and mastered the Guliang learning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read and mastered the Guliang Commentary tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 以肅睦治家，九世不異爨。

translations.literal: He governed his household with solemn harmony; nine generations shared one kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: He governed his household with solemn harmony; nine generations cooked at a single hearth.

sentences.zh: 四世孫德珪、德璋，孝友天至，晝則聯几案，夜則同衾寢。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation descendants De'gui and De'zhang possessed filial brotherhood from Heaven itself; by day they shared desks, by night they shared a blanket in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation descendants De'gui and De'zhang possessed filial brotherhood that sprang from Heaven itself; by day they shared a desk, by night they slept under the same blanket.

sentences.zh: 德璋素剛直，與物多迕，宋亡，仇家遂陷以死罪，當會逮揚州。

translations.literal: De'zhang was by nature upright and rigid and clashed with many; when Song fell, an enemy family framed him with a capital crime, and he was to be summoned and arrested in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: De'zhang was by nature upright and uncompromising and often came into conflict with others; when the Song dynasty fell, an enemy family framed him on a capital charge, and he was to be summoned and arrested in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 德珪哀弟之見誣，乃陽謂曰：「彼欲害吾也，何預爾事？

translations.literal: De'gui grieved that his brother had been falsely accused; he pretended to say to him, "They wish to harm me—what has that to do with your affair?
translations.idiomatic: De'gui grieved that his brother had been falsely accused; he pretended to say to him, "They mean to harm me—what does that have to do with you?

sentences.zh: 我往則奸狀白，爾去得不死乎！」

translations.literal: If I go the wicked deed will be exposed; if you go can you not escape death!
translations.idiomatic: If I go, the wicked plot will be exposed; if you go, how can you hope to live!

sentences.zh: 即治行。

translations.literal: Immediately he prepared to depart.
translations.idiomatic: With that he made ready to depart.

sentences.zh: 德璋追至諸暨道中，兄弟相持頓足哭，爭欲就死。

translations.literal: De'zhang caught up with him on the road to Zhuji; the brothers clung to each other, stamping their feet and weeping, each vying to go and die.
translations.idiomatic: De'zhang caught up with him on the road to Zhuji; the brothers clung to each other, stamping their feet and weeping, each insisting on going to face death in the other's place.

sentences.zh: 德珪默計沮其行，遂紿以無往，夜將半，從間道逸去。

translations.literal: De'gui silently planned to obstruct his journey; he deceived him saying he would not go, and near midnight fled by a side path.
translations.idiomatic: De'gui silently resolved to keep his brother from going; he deceived him into thinking he would not travel, and near midnight slipped away by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 德璋復追至廣陵，德珪已斃於獄。

translations.literal: De'zhang again pursued him to Guangling; De'gui had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: De'zhang pursued him again as far as Guangling, but De'gui had already died in prison.

sentences.zh: 德璋聞之，慟絕者數四，負骨歸葬。

translations.literal: When De'zhang heard it he fainted in grief several times, carried the bones home, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: When De'zhang heard the news he fainted from grief several times, then carried the bones home and buried them.

sentences.zh: 廬墓再期，每一悲號，烏鳥皆翔集不食。

translations.literal: He lived in a hut at the tomb for two mourning cycles; with each mournful cry crows and birds all flew down, gathered, and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a hut beside the tomb for two full mourning cycles; with each cry of grief crows and birds flew down, gathered around him, and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 德珪之子文嗣，幼病僂，德璋鞫之如己子。

translations.literal: De'gui's son Wensi was hunchbacked from illness in youth; De'zhang raised him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: De'gui's son Wensi had been hunchbacked since childhood; De'zhang raised him as if he were his own son.

sentences.zh: 有鮑宗岩者，字傅叔，徽州歙人。

translations.literal: There was Bao Zongyan, courtesy name Fushu, a man of She in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was Bao Zongyan, courtesy name Fushu, a native of She in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 子壽孫字子壽。

translations.literal: His son Shousun had the courtesy name Zishou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shousun had the courtesy name Zishou.

sentences.zh: 宋末，盜起里中。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, bandits rose in the village.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Song dynasty, bandits arose in their village.

sentences.zh: 宗岩避地山谷間，為賊所得，縛宗岩樹上，將殺之。

translations.literal: Zongyan fled to the mountain valleys; he was captured by bandits, tied to a tree, and they were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan fled for safety into the mountain valleys; the bandits captured him, bound him to a tree, and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 壽孫拜前願代父死，宗岩曰：「吾老矣，僅一子奉先祀，豈可殺之？

translations.literal: Shousun bowed before them and offered to die in his father's place. Zongyan said, "I am old; I have only this one son to maintain the ancestral sacrifices—how could he be killed?
translations.idiomatic: Shousun stepped forward, bowed, and offered to die in his father's place. Zongyan said, "I am old, and I have only this one son to carry on the ancestral sacrifices—how could I let him be killed?

sentences.zh: 吾願自死。」

translations.literal: I wish to die myself."
translations.idiomatic: I am the one who should die.

sentences.zh: 盜兩釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits released them both.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released them both.
